對，多數情況下我會把 Bats 當成 Bash 專案的預設推薦。因為它就是專門為 Bash 測試設計的：能測 exit code、stdout/stderr、setup/teardown、整個 test 目錄遞迴執行，還能輸出 TAP / JUnit，拿去接 CI 也很順。 ￼

但不是「任何情況都一定要上 Bats」。我通常會這樣分：

推薦用 Bats

* 這個 script 會長期維護
* 有多個行為分支、錯誤碼、參數組合
* 想放進 CI
* 想要可讀、可擴充的測試結構
* 之後可能會加 bats-assert / bats-file 這類 helper library。 ￼

不一定要用 Bats

* 只是一次性小工具
* 驗證方式很單純，跑一兩個 command 看結果就夠
* 你想要的是最少依賴、最少心智負擔
    這種情況直接寫一個 test.sh / smoke_test.sh 其實很合理。

我自己的實務建議是：

* 小型、短命 script：先用純 bash test script
* 稍微正式的 repo：直接用 Bats
* 團隊協作 / CI / 要長期維護：幾乎就是 Bats

你截圖裡那個選項我也認同，pure bash test script (Recommended) 那種做法很適合「想把測試也維持成零額外依賴、完全本地可跑」的專案；但如果你問「一般來說、通用地推哪個」，我會回答：Bats 是最穩妥的 Bash 測試標準答案。

另外我通常不會只推 Bats 本身，會一起配這三個：

* shellcheck：靜態檢查
* shfmt：格式化
* bats：行為測試

也就是：
shellcheck 管語法與壞味道，shfmt 管風格，bats 管功能正確性。

如果你想，我可以直接幫你比較：
「純 bash 測試腳本 vs Bats」 的實際差異，順便給你兩套最小模板。

下面這份可以直接拿來做選型。

先講結論

我會怎麼選

Bats

* 你主要寫 Bash
* 或你雖然寫 zsh script，但只想做黑箱測試：跑指令、看 exit code / stdout / stderr
* 想法最直覺，生態也成熟。Bats 是 Bash 測試框架，支援像 run、setup / teardown、目錄遞迴執行、TAP / JUnit 輸出。 ￼

ZUnit

* 你在做 zsh-native 的東西，例如 zsh function、plugin、autoload、zsh 特有語法
* 想要一個明確就是給 ZSH projects 的框架。 ￼

ShellSpec

* 你想支援 bash / zsh / dash / ksh / POSIX shell
* 想要更完整的測試功能，例如 BDD 風格、mocking、parameterized tests、parallel execution、coverage
* 你在乎跨 shell 的一致性。 ￼

⸻

簡化版對照

Bats

最適合：

* CLI script
* 黑箱驗證
* Bash 為主的 repo

優點：

* 很容易上手
* 社群熟
* 接 CI 很順
* 測 script 行為很自然。 ￼

缺點：

* 本體是 Bash 世界
* 測 zsh-specific function / plugin，不算最貼切

ZUnit

最適合：

* zsh plugin
* zsh function library
* 重度 zsh 語法

優點：

* 定位清楚，就是給 ZSH 用。 ￼

缺點：

* 相對沒 Bats / ShellSpec 那麼通用
* 生態與普及度通常沒那麼大

ShellSpec

最適合：

* 跨 shell 專案
* 想要功能完整的測試框架
* 想測函式、mock、coverage

優點：

* 官方直接定位成支援 dash、bash、ksh、zsh 與 POSIX shells 的 full-featured framework
* 功能比「只做簡單 command 驗證」更全面。 ￼

缺點：

* BDD 寫法一開始比較需要適應
* 對只想驗證「這個 command 有沒有成功」的人來說，可能稍重

⸻

最小可跑範例

先假設你有一個 zsh script：

#!/usr/bin/env zsh
# hello.zsh
emulate -L zsh
name="${1:-}"
if [[ -z "$name" ]]; then
  print -u2 "missing name"
  exit 2
fi
print "hello, $name"

⸻

1) 用 Bats 測 zsh script

這種最適合「黑箱測試」。

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# test/hello.bats
@test "prints greeting" {
  run zsh ./hello.zsh Alice
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ "$output" = "hello, Alice" ]
}
@test "fails without argument" {
  run zsh ./hello.zsh
  [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"missing name"* ]]
}

執行：

bats test/hello.bats

適合情境：

* 你只在乎外部行為
* 不在乎 script 內部是不是 zsh function / plugin 結構

⸻

2) 用 ZUnit 測 zsh

ZUnit 的官方定位就是 A powerful testing framework for ZSH projects，而且文件示例的語法也是 zsh 風格。安裝上官方文件提到可手動下載 / build，且需要 Revolver；把 zunit 放到 $PATH 即可。 ￼

風格大概像這樣：

#!/usr/bin/env zunit
# test/hello.zunit
@test "prints greeting" {
  run zsh ./hello.zsh Alice
  assert $state equals 0
  assert "$output" same_as "hello, Alice"
}
@test "fails without argument" {
  run zsh ./hello.zsh
  assert $state equals 2
}

手動安裝路線，官方文件提到可這樣做：

# 安裝 revolver
curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/molovo/revolver/master/revolver > /usr/local/bin/revolver
# 安裝 zunit
curl -L https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit/releases/download/__version__/zunit > /usr/local/bin/zunit
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/revolver /usr/local/bin/zunit

或從 source build：

git clone https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit
cd zunit
./build.zsh
chmod u+x ./zunit
cp ./zunit /usr/local/bin

上面安裝方式與 Revolver 依賴都來自官方文件 / repo 說明。 ￼

⸻

3) 用 ShellSpec 測 zsh

ShellSpec 最適合你想要「不只 zsh，之後可能還想測 bash / dash」的情況。它官方明確說支援 dash、bash、ksh、zsh 與 POSIX shells，並提供 mocking、parameterized tests、parallel execution、coverage 等能力。 ￼

安裝：

brew install shellspec

Homebrew 公式也明確這樣描述它。 ￼

範例：

# spec/hello_spec.sh
Describe 'hello.zsh'
  It 'prints greeting'
    When run zsh ./hello.zsh Alice
    The status should equal 0
    The output should equal "hello, Alice"
  End
  It 'fails without argument'
    When run zsh ./hello.zsh
    The status should equal 2
    The stderr should include "missing name"
  End
End

執行：

shellspec

這種寫法很像 RSpec / BDD，讀起來很像規格書。

⸻

真正實務上怎麼挑

選 Bats，如果你：

* 已經會 Bats
* 主要測 command behavior
* 希望團隊成員一眼就懂
* 不想導入新測試語法

選 ZUnit，如果你：

* 在做 zsh plugin / dotfiles / autoload function
* 希望語境完全在 zsh 裡
* 覺得「拿 Bash 框架測 zsh」不夠貼身

選 ShellSpec，如果你：

* 要跨 shell
* 要 mock / coverage / 更完整功能
* 想把 shell 測試做成比較正式的工程流程。 ￼

⸻

我自己的推薦

如果你現在是一般工程情境，我會這樣建議：

* Bash repo → 直接 Bats
* zsh plugin / zsh-heavy repo → 先看 ShellSpec，再考慮 ZUnit
* 只是 zsh interpreter 的 CLI script → Bats 就夠了

一句話版：

* 最省事：Bats
* 最 zsh 專用：ZUnit
* 最完整、最通用：ShellSpec

如果你要，我下一則可以直接幫你做一份
「zsh 專案測試模板」，分別給你：

1. Bats 版
2. ShellSpec 版
3. 適合 dotfiles / plugin 的目錄結構。
```

2. Zsh proxy logic (used daily; failures are hard to debug)

- Pure logic concentrated in specific files = isolated, testable
- High-value regression prevention (secrets, proxy, git)
- Low setup friction (no chezmoi API mocking, no network mocks needed)
- Can run without system state

74	    return 1

79	    return 1

84	          set -e
85	          if ! command -v tic >/dev/null 2>&1; then
86	            echo "remote: tic not found" >&2
87	            exit 127
88	          fi
89	          mkdir -p "$HOME/.terminfo"
90	          TERMINFO="$HOME/.terminfo" tic -x -
91	        ' 2> >(grep -Fv "older tic versions may treat the description field as an alias" >&2); then
92	    echo "ghostty-ssh-terminfo: failed to install on $host" >&2
93	    return 1
94	  fi

65	# --- Proxy helpers (generic) ---
66	# Portable proxy management: honor $LOCAL_PROXY_URL, else auto-probe common
67	# loopback ports (Clash 7890/7891, ClashX 1087, Privoxy 8118, generic 8080).
68	# Detection result is cached per-shell in _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE; use
69	# `proxy-refresh` after starting/stopping the proxy.
70	#
71	# Environment variables honored:
72	#   LOCAL_PROXY_URL         HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890).
73	#                           If unset, ports are auto-probed.
74	#   LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL   Optional separate SOCKS5 endpoint (e.g.
75	#                           socks5://127.0.0.1:7891). Used for ALL_PROXY /
76	#                           all_proxy when set; otherwise these fall back to
77	#                           LOCAL_PROXY_URL / the probe result. Useful when
78	#                           Clash is configured with split `port:` and
79	#                           `socks-port:` instead of `mixed-port:`.
80	#   LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1  Run `proxy-on` silently at shell startup
81	#                           whenever a proxy is detected. Handy on machines
82	#                           that always route through the local proxy.
83	
84	: "${_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE:=}"
85	__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS=(7890 7891 1087 8118 8080)
86	
87	__zsh_net_detect_proxy() {
88	  [[ -n "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]] && return 0
89	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" ]]; then
90	    _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="$LOCAL_PROXY_URL"
91	    return 0
92	  fi
93	  local port
94	  for port in "${__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[@]}"; do
95	    if nc -z -w1 127.0.0.1 "$port" 2>/dev/null; then
96	      _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="http://127.0.0.1:$port"
97	      return 0
98	    fi
99	  done
100	  _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="none"
101	  return 1
102	}
103	
104	# Resolve the URL that should be used for ALL_PROXY / all_proxy.
105	# Falls back to the HTTP proxy when no SOCKS-specific URL is set (works for
106	# mixed-port Clash configs where one port serves both HTTP and SOCKS).
107	__zsh_net_all_proxy_url() {
108	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]]; then
109	    print -r -- "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL"
110	  else
111	    print -r -- "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE"
112	  fi
113	}
114	
115	# Run one command with proxy env applied to the child process only.
116	withproxy() {
117	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
118	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
119	    "$@"
120	    return
121	  fi
122	  local all_url
123	  all_url="$(__zsh_net_all_proxy_url)"
124	  http_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
125	  https_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
126	  HTTP_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
127	  HTTPS_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
128	  ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
129	  all_proxy="$all_url" \
130	    "$@"
131	}
132	
133	# Run direct first; on non-zero exit, retry via proxy if one is available.
134	try_direct_then_proxy() {
135	  "$@" && return 0
136	  local rc=$?
137	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
138	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
139	    return $rc
140	  fi
141	  print -u2 "[retry via proxy $_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE]"
142	  withproxy "$@"
143	}
144	
145	# Export proxy env vars to the current shell (all downstream commands inherit).
146	# If $1 is "-q", suppress the success message (used by auto-activate).
147	proxy-on() {
148	  local quiet=0
149	  [[ "$1" == "-q" ]] && quiet=1
150	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
151	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
152	    (( quiet )) || print -u2 "proxy-on: no proxy detected (set \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL or start your proxy, then \`proxy-refresh\`)"
153	    return 1
154	  fi
155	  local all_url
156	  all_url="$(__zsh_net_all_proxy_url)"
157	  export http_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
158	         https_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
159	         HTTP_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
160	         HTTPS_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
161	         ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
162	         all_proxy="$all_url"
163	  if (( ! quiet )); then
164	    if [[ "$all_url" == "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]]; then
165	      print "proxy ON  ->  $_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE"
166	    else
167	      print "proxy ON  ->  http/https=$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE  all/socks=$all_url"
168	    fi
169	  fi
170	}
171	
172	# Unset all proxy env vars from the current shell.
173	proxy-off() {
174	  unset http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy
175	  print "proxy OFF"
176	}
177	
178	# Report current proxy state: active / available / unavailable.
179	proxy-status() {
180	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
181	  local shell_active=""
182	  if [[ -n "$http_proxy$https_proxy$ALL_PROXY" ]]; then
183	    shell_active="yes"
184	  fi
185	  local source="probe"
186	  [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" ]] && source="LOCAL_PROXY_URL env"
187	
188	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
189	    print "proxy: unavailable (no \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL; no loopback port from ${__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[*]} reachable)"
190	    [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && print "  note: shell env still has proxy vars set -- run \`proxy-off\` to clear"
191	    return 1
192	  fi
193	
194	  local state="available"
195	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && state="active   "
196	  local hint="(not exported; use \`withproxy\`, \`try_direct_then_proxy\`, or \`proxy-on\`)"
197	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && hint="(exported in current shell)"
198	
199	  print "proxy: $state http=$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE  source=$source  $hint"
200	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]]; then
201	    print "  socks=$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL  source=LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL env"
202	  fi
203	}
204	
205	# Clear the cached detection and re-probe; call after toggling your proxy.
206	proxy-refresh() {
207	  _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE=""
208	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
209	  proxy-status
210	}
211	
212	# Optional auto-activation: when $LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1 is set before
213	# this file is sourced, silently call `proxy-on` if a proxy is detected.
214	# Set the env var in a machine-local zsh file (or ~/.zshenv) on machines that
215	# should always route through the loopback proxy.
216	if [[ "$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE" == "1" ]]; then
217	  proxy-on -q
218	fi

 `./dot_config/zsh/tools/11_tools_picker.zsh`

```text
1	# 11_tools_picker.zsh - Interactive CLI tools picker (fzf ZLE widget)
2	# Reads ~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md for the tool list (deployed by chezmoi).
3	#
4	# Alt+T  →  open picker
5	#   Enter      paste invocation to shell buffer (you still press Enter to run)
6	#   Ctrl+E     execute the tool directly (good for TUI apps: btop, lazygit, etc.)
7	#   Ctrl+/     toggle preview panel (shows tldr or --help)
8	#
9	# The invocation for tools that need arguments has a trailing space,
10	# so pressing Enter pastes e.g. "rg " — cursor lands after the space,
11	# ready for you to type your arguments.
12	
13	_TOOLS_DOC="${HOME}/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md"
14	
15	# Bail silently if the data file hasn't been deployed yet or fzf is missing
16	[[ -f "$_TOOLS_DOC" ]] || return 0
17	command -v fzf &>/dev/null || return 0
18	
19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.
20	# Tab separator preserves the trailing space in invocations like "rg ".
21	_tools_list() {
22	    awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
23	      inv=$3; sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/,"",inv); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/,"",inv)
24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)
25	      printf "%s\t%s\n", inv, desc
26	    }' "$_TOOLS_DOC"
27	}
28	
29	# ZLE widget: opens fzf picker, pastes selected invocation to the shell command line.
30	tools-picker() {
31	    {
32	        exec </dev/tty
33	        exec <&1
34	
35	        local selected
36	        selected=$(
37	            _tools_list | fzf \
38	                --ansi \
39	                --border \
40	                --prompt ' tools  ' \
41	                --header 'Enter: paste  Ctrl+E: execute  Ctrl+/: preview' \
42	                --delimiter=$'\t' \
43	                --with-nth=1,2 \
44	                --preview 'tool=$(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}" | sed "s/ *$//"); (command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1 && tldr "$tool" 2>/dev/null) || "$tool" --help 2>&1 | head -50' \
45	                --preview-window='right:55%:wrap:hidden' \
46	                --bind='ctrl-/:toggle-preview' \
47	                --bind='ctrl-e:execute(eval $(printf "%s" {1} | awk "{print \$1}"))+abort'
48	        )
49	
50	        zle reset-prompt >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
51	        [[ -z "$selected" ]] && return
52	
53	        # Extract the invocation (field 1 before the tab), preserving trailing space
54	        local invocation
55	        invocation=$(printf '%s' "$selected" | cut -f1)
56	
57	        # Paste to shell command line buffer without executing
58	        LBUFFER="${LBUFFER}${invocation}"
59	        zle redisplay
60	    }
61	}
62	
63	zle -N tools-picker
64	
65	# Alt+T (mnemonic: Tools)
66	# Alt+S = sesh-sessions, Alt+C = fzf cd — Alt+T is free
67	bindkey -M emacs '\et' tools-picker
68	bindkey -M viins '\et' tools-picker
69	bindkey -M vicmd '\et' tools-picker
70
```

192	#      `-e @file` so subsequent invocations (partial-failure loop) don't re-prompt.
193	#   3. If neither works, print a clear manual command and exit 0 (don't break
194	#      the rest of `chezmoi apply`).
195	sudo -k 2>/dev/null || true
196	if sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
197	    info "Passwordless sudo detected"
198	    BECOME_FLAGS=""
199	elif [[ -r /dev/tty && -w /dev/tty ]]; then
200	    info "Sudo password required - reading once from /dev/tty"
201	    BECOME_PASS_FILE="$(mktemp)"
202	    chmod 600 "$BECOME_PASS_FILE"
203	    trap 'rm -f "$BECOME_PASS_FILE"' EXIT
204	    printf "[sudo] password for %s: " "$USER" > /dev/tty
205	    IFS= read -rs SUDO_PASS < /dev/tty
206	    echo > /dev/tty
207	    # Write as ansible vars file so password never appears in argv / ps / history.
208	    # Use printf with %s (no shell interpretation) and escape embedded double quotes.
209	    ESCAPED_PASS="${SUDO_PASS//\"/\\\"}"
210	    printf 'ansible_become_password: "%s"\n' "$ESCAPED_PASS" > "$BECOME_PASS_FILE"
211	    unset SUDO_PASS ESCAPED_PASS
212	    BECOME_FLAGS="-e @$BECOME_PASS_FILE"
213	else
214	    warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo and no /dev/tty access"
215	    warn "Skipping ansible run. To complete setup, run manually:"
216	    warn ""
217	    warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini \\"
218	    warn "    $PLAYBOOK \\"
219	    warn "    --tags '$TAGS' --ask-become-pass"
220	    warn ""
221	    warn "Or grant passwordless sudo:"
222	    warn "  echo '$USER ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/$USER"
223	    exit 0
224	fi
225	{{ end -}}
226	{{ end -}}
227	
228	info "Profile: {{ .profile }}"
229	info "Re-running ansible with tags: $TAGS"
230	EXTRA_VARS_ARGS=()
231	[[ -n "$EXTRA_VARS" ]] && EXTRA_VARS_ARGS=(--extra-vars "$EXTRA_VARS")
232	
233	{{ $allowPartialFailure := false }}{{ if hasKey . "allowPartialFailure" }}{{ $allowPartialFailure = .allowPartialFailure }}{{ end -}}
234	{{ if $allowPartialFailure -}}
235	# Best-effort mode: run each tag separately so one failure doesn't block others
236	info "allowPartialFailure=true: running each tag independently"
237	FAILED_TAGS=()
238	IFS=',' read -ra TAG_ARRAY <<< "$TAGS"
239	for tag in "${TAG_ARRAY[@]}"; do
240	    info "────── Running tag: $tag ──────"
241	    ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$tag" $BECOME_FLAGS "${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[@]}" || {
242	        warn "Tag '$tag' had failures (continuing in best-effort mode)"
243	        FAILED_TAGS+=("$tag")
244	    }
245	done
246	if [[ ${#FAILED_TAGS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
247	    warn "────── Summary ──────"
248	    warn "The following tags had failures: ${FAILED_TAGS[*]}"
249	    warn "Retry manually:"
250	    warn "  cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook -i inventories/localhost.ini $PLAYBOOK --tags '$(IFS=,; echo "${FAILED_TAGS[*]}")' $BECOME_FLAGS ${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[*]}"
251	    success "Ansible roles partially updated (${#FAILED_TAGS[@]} tag(s) failed)."
252	else
253	    success "Ansible roles updated!"
254	fi
255	{{ else -}}
256	ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$TAGS" $BECOME_FLAGS "${EXTRA_VARS_ARGS[@]}"
257	success "Ansible roles updated!"
258	{{ end -}}

```text
1	# Dotfiles Repository
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles management using **chezmoi** for configuration files and **ansible** for system dependencies.
4	
5	## Maintaining README.md
6	
7	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying configurations, update `README.md` to reflect changes:
8	
9	- **New config files**: Add to "What You Get > Config Files" section
10	- **New ansible roles/tools**: Add to "What You Get > Tools" section
11	- **New platforms**: Add to "Supported Platforms" table
12	- **Changed setup steps**: Update "Quick Setup" section
13	
14	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong in CLAUDE.md or docs/.
15	
16	## Maintaining Custom Aliases & Shell Functions
17	
18	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update `docs/zsh/aliases.md`:
19	
20	- **New entry**: add a row with the command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description
21	- **Modified entry**: update the existing row to reflect changes
22	- **Removed entry**: delete the row
23	
24	This keeps `docs/zsh/aliases.md` as the single quick-reference for all custom shell shortcuts.
25	
26	## Maintaining Dockerfile
27	
28	**IMPORTANT**: When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, also update `Dockerfile`:
29	
30	1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument
31	2. Add `--promptBool` or `--promptString` flag to the `chezmoi init` command
32	
33	This ensures Docker testing works with all configuration options.
34	
35	## Maintaining Keyboard Shortcuts
36	
37	**IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying keybindings in any tool config, cross-check against other tools to avoid conflicts. Multiple tools share the terminal's key namespace — especially `Ctrl+` and `Alt+` modifiers.
38	
39	**Conflict surfaces to check:**
40	
41	| Tool | Config file | Key conflict risk |
42	|------|-------------|-------------------|
43	| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch) |
44	| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
45	| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` override global |
46	| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
47	| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
48	
49	**Known conflict zones:**
50	
51	- `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` — tmux vim-tmux-navigator pane navigation; removed/remapped in TV global config
52	- `Ctrl+S/F/R` — TV built-in cycling/reload; avoid in channel actions
53	- `Alt+*` — safe namespace for channel-specific actions (used by pueue channel); requires terminal to send Option as Meta
54	
55	**Resolution precedence:** tmux root-table bindings intercept keys before they reach the inner application. When running TV inside tmux, any `bind-key -n C-*` in tmux will shadow the same `ctrl-*` in TV. Prefer `Alt+` for custom actions to avoid this entirely.
56	
57	## Quick Start
58	
59	```bash
60	# Install ansible (if not already installed)
61	uv tool install ansible-core
62	ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
63	
64	# Apply dotfiles
65	chezmoi apply
66	
67	# Run ansible manually (from ~/.ansible directory)
68	cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
69	```
70	
71	## Architecture
72	
73	```
74	chezmoi repo/
75	├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
76	├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
77	├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
78	└── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
79	```
80	
81	Installation Order:
82	
83	```
84	1. Bootstrap (run_once_before) - installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise
85	2. chezmoi apply - deploys config files + ansible playbooks
86	3. Ansible (run_onchange_after) - runs on fresh install + when roles change
87	4. Brew bundle (run_onchange_after) - installs GUI apps if enabled
88	```
89	
90	### Auto-run Scripts
91	
92	| Script | Behavior |
93	|--------|----------|
94	| `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
95	| `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
96	| `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled) |
97	
98	The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs:
99	
100	- **Fresh install**: no previous hash state → triggers run
101	- **Updates**: any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes → triggers run
102	
103	To force re-run all scripts:
104	
105	```bash
106	chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
107	chezmoi apply
108	```
109	
110	## Chezmoi Commands
111	
112	```bash
113	chezmoi diff              # Preview changes
114	chezmoi apply             # Apply changes
115	chezmoi apply --dry-run   # Test without applying
116	chezmoi edit <file>       # Edit source file
117	chezmoi cd                # Go to source directory
118	```
119	
120	## Ansible Usage
121	
122	Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/` directory:
123	
124	```bash
125	cd ~/.ansible
126	
127	# Full setup (macOS)
128	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
129	
130	# Full setup (Linux)
131	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml
132	
133	# Specific tags only
134	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
135	
136	# Skip tags requiring sudo
137	ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo"
138	
139	# Dry run
140	ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check
141	```
142	
143	### Available Tags
144	
145	| Tag | Description |
146	|-----|-------------|
147	| `base` | git, git-lfs, curl, ripgrep, fd, build tools |
148	| `homebrew` | macOS Homebrew update (installation done by bootstrap) |
149	| `zsh` | zsh, oh-my-zsh, plugins (autosuggestions, syntax-highlighting, completions) |
150	| `starship` | Starship cross-shell prompt (replaces oh-my-zsh theme) |
151	| `neovim` | Neovim (>= 0.11.2) |
152	| `lazyvim_deps` | fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js (via mise) |

167	## Profiles
168	
169	| Profile | OS | Tags Included |
170	|---------|-----|---------------|
171	| `macos` | macOS | homebrew, base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, nerdfonts, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools, alacritty |
172	| `ubuntu_desktop` | Ubuntu | base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, nerdfonts, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools, alacritty |
173	| `ubuntu_server` | Ubuntu | base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools |
174	
175	**Tag categories:**
176	
177	- **Core** (all): base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, security_tools
178	- **Desktop** (macos, ubuntu_desktop): nerdfonts
179	- **macOS only**: homebrew
180	- **Optional** (via chezmoi config): coding_agents, bitwarden, python_uv_tools, llm_tools, input_method (desktop only), networking_tools
181	
182	Note: `ubuntu_server` excludes `nerdfonts` (no GUI needed).
183	
184	## No Root Mode (Linux)
185	
186	For Linux servers where you don't have sudo/root access, enable `noRoot = true` during `chezmoi init`:
187	
188	```bash
189	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "No sudo/root access" prompt
190	```
191	
192	This skips all tasks tagged with `[sudo]` (apt packages, system-level installations). Tools with user-level fallbacks are automatically installed to `~/.local/bin` instead.
193	
194	**User-level tools** (installed automatically without sudo):
195	
196	- **GitHub binaries**: neovim, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, bats, eza, delta, yazi, superfile, zellij, btop, gitleaks, lazygit, fzf, sesh, taplo, television
197	- **tmux-appimage** (x86_64 only): extracted AppImage → `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root`, shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`. Runs only when the system `tmux` is older than 3.3 (see "tmux version requirement" below).
198	- **mise**: Node.js, Rust runtime management
199	- **Installers**: zoxide, starship, pre-commit, thefuck, tldr
200	- **cargo tools**: pueue
201	- **uv tools**: mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.
202	- **llm tools**: ollama, litellm, llmfit, models
203	- **npm tools**: Claude Code, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Bitwarden CLI, etc.
204	
205	What you **won't get** without root:
206	
207	- zsh (needs `/etc/shells` for login shell)
208	- htop (requires system libraries)
209	- direnv (apt only)
210	- Docker (kernel features, daemon)
211	- Ollama (system service install)
212	- System fonts (nerdfonts)
213	- Ruby and gem tools (ruby-build requires `libffi-dev` which needs sudo)
214	- build-essential, git, curl, wget, tree (assumed pre-installed)
215	
216	**Tip**: Ask your sysadmin to run: `sudo apt install git curl wget zsh tmux htop direnv build-essential tree`
217	
218	## ARM / Raspberry Pi Support
219	
220	Raspberry Pi 5 (64-bit OS only) works with the `ubuntu_server` profile and gets full tool support. Raspberry Pi 4 may run 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS (armhf userland) with a 64-bit kernel (`arm_64bit=1` default), which causes `uname -m` to report `aarch64` while userland is 32-bit.
221	
222	**How it's handled:**
223	
224	- **Bootstrap**: Detects userland architecture via `dpkg --print-architecture`; skips Linuxbrew on armhf (Homebrew requires amd64 or arm64 userland)
225	- **Ansible playbooks**: `linux.yml` has `pre_tasks` that override `ansible_architecture` to match the real userland (e.g. `armv7l` instead of `aarch64`), so roles download correct binaries
226	- **Tool availability on armhf (32-bit ARM)**: apt packages work fine; GitHub release downloads are skipped for tools without armv7l builds
227	
228	**Tools with armv7l/armhf releases** (work on RPi 4 32-bit): ripgrep, fd, jq, glow, rclone, direnv, gitleaks, trippy, speedtest, bats (pure-bash, arch-agnostic)
229	
230	**Tools skipped on armv7l** (no 32-bit ARM release): neovim (GitHub tarball), lazygit, eza, git-delta, yazi, superfile, zellij, sesh, taplo, television, duckdb, doggo, gping, bandwhich, SpecStory, CodexBar, Claude Code (install.sh ships arm64/amd64 only)
231	
232	**Tools skipped on armv7l via mise** (no armv7l prebuilt): bun, ruby; node pinned to `node@20` (last LTS with armv7l tarball). npm-based tools (tldr, etc.) install via `mise exec -- npm` and work on armv7l. tree-sitter-cli is still skipped (cargo build needs libclang and takes 15+ min on RPi 4).
233	
234	**Recommendation**: Use 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS for full tool compatibility.
235	
236	## Tmux Configuration
237	
238	**Minimum version: tmux >= 3.3.** The popup menu on `prefix + Space` uses `display-menu -x R -y P`; tmux 3.2a places the menu past the terminal edge and silently suppresses it ("_If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed._"), while 3.3+ clamps the position. The Ansible `devtools` role detects old tmux on Debian/Ubuntu and upgrades automatically: Linuxbrew when present, otherwise a user-level install of [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`. After the upgrade, run `tmux kill-server` once so existing sessions switch over to the new binary (running servers keep the old binary in memory).
239	
240	The tmux config is modular under `dot_config/tmux/` (deployed to `~/.config/tmux/`), with `dot_tmux.conf` acting as a one-line shim at `~/.tmux.conf`. Structure: `tmux.conf` (entry point + theme selector), `common.conf` (plugins, general options, terminal compat), `keybindings.conf` (all binds + popup menu), `theme.catppuccin.conf` (default, top status bar), `theme.tmux2k.conf` (alternative, bottom bar).
241	
242	Theme selection priority: `$TMUX_THEME` env var → `@theme_variant` tmux option → default `catppuccin`. Switch at runtime with `prefix + M-c` (Catppuccin) or `prefix + M-t` (tmux2k). See `docs/tools/tmux/` (README, keybindings, themes, vim) for full details, including a troubleshooting note on the tmux2k bandwidth segment (`18446744073709551615K` = uint64 underflow).
243	
244	The Catppuccin status bar is **responsive**: `responsive.sh` + a `client-resized` hook dynamically adjust which modules are shown based on terminal width (>= 120 full, 80-119 medium, < 80 minimal). This makes the status bar usable on mobile terminals. See `docs/tools/tmux/themes.md` for details.
245	
246	### Key Settings for Coding Agents
247	
248	- `extended-keys always` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` -- forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, etc. through tmux to inner applications (Claude Code, Neovim, etc.)
249	- `escape-time 0` -- eliminates ESC delay for Neovim
250	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) -- OSC 52 clipboard works over SSH without relying on terminfo `Ms`. Paired with an SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` so remote Neovim yanks reach the local clipboard. See `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` → "OSC 52 Clipboard" for verification steps.
251	- `allow-passthrough on` -- OSC passthrough for terminal images
252	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See `docs/tools/ghostty.md`.
253	
254	### Tmux Keybindings
255	
256	| Binding | Action |
257	|---------|--------|
258	| `Ctrl + 1..9` | Switch to window 1–9 (no prefix, requires CSI-u terminal) |
259	| `Ctrl + 0` | Jump to git root session via sesh (no prefix, requires CSI-u) |
260	| `prefix + Space` | Native popup menu (layouts, sessions, sesh, resize, etc.) |
261	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | Navigate panes (vim-style) |
262	| `prefix + H/J/K/L` | Resize panes (5 cells) |
263	| `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` | Fine resize panes (1 cell) |
264	| `prefix + +` | Set current pane to 75% width |
265	| `prefix + \|` | Split pane left/right |
266	| `prefix + -` | Split pane top/bottom |
267	| `prefix + F` | Toggle floating pane (tmux-floax) |
268	| `prefix + P` | Floax popup menu |
269	| `prefix + u` | Open fzf URL picker (tmux-fzf-url) |
270	| `prefix + [` | Enter vim-style copy mode (v/V/y to select/yank) |
271	| `prefix + y` | Copy visible pane to clipboard |
272	| `prefix + Y` | Copy full scrollback to clipboard |
273	| `prefix + C-y` | fzf line picker from scrollback |
274	| `prefix + g` | Sesh session picker (fzf popup) |
275	| `prefix + T` | Sesh session picker (television popup) |
276	| `prefix + O` | Sesh built-in picker popup |
277	| `prefix + W` | Sesh window picker (fzf popup) |
278	| `prefix + S` | Switch to last session (sesh) |
279	| `prefix + 9` | Jump to git root session (sesh) |
280	| `prefix + N` | New session (prompts for name) |
281	| `prefix + X` | Kill session (with confirmation) |
282	| `prefix + M` | Move window to another session (tab tear-out) |
283	| `prefix + B` | Break pane into new window in another session |
284	| `prefix + A` | Link window into another session (shared, not copied) |
285	| `prefix + R` | Reload tmux config |
286	| `prefix + M-c` | Switch theme to Catppuccin (top status bar) |
287	| `prefix + M-t` | Switch theme to tmux2k (bottom status bar) |
288	
289	Note: `Ctrl+Space` is NOT bound (reserved for input method switching). `Ctrl+1..9` and `Ctrl+0` require CSI-u terminal support (Ghostty/cmux, Alacritty, Kitty); legacy terminals fall back to `prefix + number`. Popup menu accelerator keys match standalone `prefix + key` bindings (see `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md` for full mapping).
290	
291	## Zellij Configuration
292	
293	Zellij config (`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl`) uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications.
294	
295	On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset for the best experience.
296	
297	## LazyVim Requirements
298	
299	- Neovim >= 0.11.2
300	- ripgrep, fd
301	- Node.js (via mise on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)
302	- tree-sitter-cli
303	- lazygit, fzf (via git on Linux, Homebrew on macOS)

305	## Directory Structure
306	
307	After `chezmoi apply`:
308	
309	- Config files in `~/.*`
310	- Ansible playbooks in `~/.ansible/`

312	## Development
313	
314	After modifying ansible playbooks or roles, run syntax check:
315	
316	```bash
317	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/base.yml
318	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/macos.yml
319	ANSIBLE_CONFIG=dot_ansible/ansible.cfg ansible-playbook --syntax-check dot_ansible/playbooks/linux.yml
320	```
321	
322	## Ansible vs Homebrew
323	
324	**Primary tool: Ansible** - manages CLI tools and system dependencies cross-platform.
325	
326	| Tool | Role | When to Use |
327	|------|------|-------------|
328	| **Ansible** | CLI tools, system packages | Always (apt/brew formulas) |
329	| **Brewfile** | macOS GUI apps (casks), App Store | Optional (opt-in) |
330	| **Linuxbrew** | Linux packages not in apt | Always installed on Linux |
331	
332	**How they work together:**
333	
334	- Bootstrap installs Homebrew on both macOS and Linux
335	- Ansible roles use `community.general.homebrew` for macOS formulas
336	- Brewfile manages casks (GUI apps) and mas (App Store) separately
337	- On Linux, Ansible uses apt; Linuxbrew is available for newer packages
338	
339	For a deeper comparison of Linux package sources (apt / snap / Linuxbrew / GitHub binaries) and the policy the ansible roles follow when picking between them, see [docs/linux-package-sources.md](docs/linux-package-sources.md).
340	
341	## Brewfile (GUI Apps - Opt-in)
342	
343	GUI applications are managed via Homebrew Brewfile in XDG-compliant location `~/.config/homebrew/`.
344	
345	**Note**: Brewfile installation is **opt-in** (disabled by default). Enable general GUI apps via `chezmoi init --force` and set `installBrewApps = true`. On macOS, AI desktop apps are a separate opt-in via `installAiDesktopApps = true`.
346	
347	### File Structure
348	
349	```
350	~/.config/homebrew/
351	├── Brewfile          # Shared: taps, CLI formulas, mas
352	├── Brewfile.darwin   # macOS: casks (GUI apps), mas entries
353	└── Brewfile.linux    # Linux: linuxbrew-specific (minimal)
354	```
355	
356	### Usage
357	
358	```bash
359	# Edit Brewfiles
360	chezmoi edit ~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
361	
362	# Apply changes manually
363	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile
364	brew bundle --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
365	
366	# Or just run chezmoi apply (triggers run_onchange script)
367	chezmoi apply
368	
369	# Check what would be installed
370	brew bundle check --file=~/.config/homebrew/Brewfile.darwin
371	```
372	
373	### Brewfile Categories (darwin)
374	
375	- **Terminals & Editors**: alacritty, iterm2, warp, cmux, cursor, visual-studio-code
376	- **AI & Coding**: claude, chatgpt, opencode-desktop, antigravity, codex-app (Apple Silicon only), and `ollama-app` when `installAiDesktopApps` + `installLlmTools`
377	- **System Utilities**: aerospace, alt-tab, raycast, jordanbaird-ice
378	- **Communication**: discord, telegram, wechat, tencent-meeting
379	- **Browsers**: arc, google-chrome, tor-browser
380	- **Productivity**: obsidian, google-drive, grammarly-desktop
381	- **Gaming**: steam, minecraft, battle-net (skipped if WORK_MACHINE env var set)
382	- **Finance**: binance, tradingview
383	- **Network**: tailscale, openvpn-connect, clash-verge-rev
384	- **Mac App Store**: LINE, Keynote, Numbers, Pages
385	
386	### Customizing Brewfile
387	
388	The Brewfiles are chezmoi templates. Conditional sections:
389	
390	- Gaming apps: skipped if `WORK_MACHINE` environment variable is set
391	- Chinese apps (baidunetdisk): only included if `useChineseMirror` is true
392	- mas apps: requires signing in to App Store.app first
393	
394	## Customization
395	
396	See [docs/ansible.md](docs/ansible.md) for detailed ansible customization guide.

```text
# Dotfiles test/devbox container
# Build: docker build -t dotfiles .
# Run:   docker run -it dotfiles

FROM ubuntu:24.04

# Build arguments for chezmoi configuration
ARG CHEZMOI_PROFILE=ubuntu_server
ARG CHEZMOI_EMAIL=docker@example.com
ARG CHEZMOI_NAME="Docker User"
ARG CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR=false
ARG CHEZMOI_GITLEAKS_ALL_REPOS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_CODING_AGENTS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BITWARDEN=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_PYTHON_UV_TOOLS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_LLM_TOOLS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_AI_DESKTOP_APPS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BREW_APPS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_INPUT_METHOD=false
ARG CHEZMOI_INSTALL_NETWORKING_TOOLS=false
ARG CHEZMOI_NO_ROOT=false
ARG CHEZMOI_BACKUP_DOTFILES=false
ARG CHEZMOI_ALLOW_PARTIAL_FAILURE=false
ARG CHEZMOI_REPO=daviddwlee84

# Avoid interactive prompts during apt install
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure HTTP mirror BEFORE installing ca-certificates (if in China)
# This solves the chicken-and-egg problem: HTTPS mirrors need ca-certificates,
# but installing ca-certificates from default repos fails under GFW
# Uses HTTP (not HTTPS) since ca-certificates isn't installed yet
RUN if [ "${CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR}" = "true" ]; then \
        ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
        if [ "$ARCH" = "amd64" ]; then \
            MIRROR_URL="http://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu"; \
        else \
            MIRROR_URL="http://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu-ports"; \
        fi && \
        printf '%s\n' \
            "Types: deb" \
            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \
            "Suites: noble noble-updates noble-backports" \
            "Components: main restricted universe multiverse" \
            "Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg" \
            "" \
            "Types: deb" \
            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \
            "Suites: noble-security" \
            "Components: main restricted universe multiverse" \
            "Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg" \
            > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources; \
    fi

# Install ca-certificates (now using HTTP mirror if in China, default repos otherwise)
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Upgrade to HTTPS mirror after ca-certificates is installed (if in China)
# HTTPS is more secure for subsequent package installations
RUN if [ "${CHEZMOI_USE_CHINESE_MIRROR}" = "true" ]; then \
        ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
        if [ "$ARCH" = "amd64" ]; then \
            MIRROR_URL="https://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu"; \
        else \
            MIRROR_URL="https://repo.huaweicloud.com/ubuntu-ports"; \
        fi && \
        printf '%s\n' \
            "Types: deb" \
            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \
            "Suites: noble noble-updates noble-backports" \
            "Components: main restricted universe multiverse" \
            "Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg" \
            "" \
            "Types: deb" \
            "URIs: ${MIRROR_URL}" \
            "Suites: noble-security" \
            "Components: main restricted universe multiverse" \
            "Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg" \
            > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources; \
    fi

# Install minimal dependencies
# python3 is required for ansible to run modules on localhost
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    curl \
    sudo \
    git \
    python3 \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Create non-root user with sudo access
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash devuser \
    && echo "devuser ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" >> /etc/sudoers.d/devuser \
    && chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/devuser

# Copy local dotfiles source into image
# This allows testing local changes without pushing to GitHub
COPY --chown=devuser:devuser . /tmp/dotfiles-source
```

10	對，多數情況下我會把 **Bats 當成 Bash 專案的預設推薦**。因為它就是專門為 Bash 測試設計的：能測 exit code、stdout/stderr、setup/teardown、整個 test 目錄遞迴執行，還能輸出 TAP / JUnit，拿去接 CI 也很順。([bats-core.readthedocs.io][1])
11	
12	但不是「任何情況都一定要上 Bats」。我通常會這樣分：
13	
14	**推薦用 Bats**
15	
16	* 這個 script 會長期維護
17	* 有多個行為分支、錯誤碼、參數組合
18	* 想放進 CI
19	* 想要可讀、可擴充的測試結構
20	* 之後可能會加 `bats-assert` / `bats-file` 這類 helper library。([bats-core.readthedocs.io][2])
21	
22	**不一定要用 Bats**
23	
24	* 只是一次性小工具
25	* 驗證方式很單純，跑一兩個 command 看結果就夠
26	* 你想要的是最少依賴、最少心智負擔
27	  這種情況直接寫一個 `test.sh` / `smoke_test.sh` 其實很合理。
28	
29	我自己的實務建議是：
30	
31	* **小型、短命 script**：先用純 bash test script
32	* **稍微正式的 repo**：直接用 Bats
33	* **團隊協作 / CI / 要長期維護**：幾乎就是 Bats
34	
35	你截圖裡那個選項我也認同，`pure bash test script (Recommended)` 那種做法很適合「想把測試也維持成零額外依賴、完全本地可跑」的專案；但如果你問「一般來說、通用地推哪個」，我會回答：**Bats 是最穩妥的 Bash 測試標準答案**。
36	
37	另外我通常不會只推 Bats 本身，會一起配這三個：
38	
39	* `shellcheck`：靜態檢查
40	* `shfmt`：格式化
41	* `bats`：行為測試
42	
43	也就是：
44	**shellcheck 管語法與壞味道，shfmt 管風格，bats 管功能正確性。**
45	
46	如果你想，我可以直接幫你比較：
47	**「純 bash 測試腳本 vs Bats」** 的實際差異，順便給你兩套最小模板。

50	[2]: https://bats-core.readthedocs.io/en/stable/writing-tests.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Writing tests - bats-core's documentation! - Read the Docs"
51

6	"""
7	Check for secrets in .specstory/history/ files using gitleaks and
8	detect-private-key patterns. Reports findings and suggests redaction.

10	Usage:
11	    ./scripts/redact_specstory.py              # Check staged files (default)
12	    ./scripts/redact_specstory.py --fix        # Auto-redact and re-stage files
13	    ./scripts/redact_specstory.py --working-dir  # Scan working directory instead of staged

15	import argparse
16	import json
17	import re
18	import subprocess
19	import sys

21	from pathlib import Path

23	
24	def read_text(path: Path) -> str:
25	    """Read as UTF-8 while preserving invalid bytes via surrogate escape."""
26	    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
27	
28	
29	def write_text(path: Path, content: str) -> None:
30	    """Write UTF-8 while preserving surrogate-escaped bytes."""
31	    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape")
32	
33	
34	def run_gitleaks_staged() -> list[dict]:
35	    """Run gitleaks on staged files and return findings as JSON."""
36	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=".json", delete=False) as f:
37	        report_path = f.name
38	
39	    try:
40	        subprocess.run(
41	            [
42	                "gitleaks",
43	                "protect",
44	                "--staged",
45	                "--report-format",
46	                "json",
47	                "--report-path",
48	                report_path,
49	                "--exit-code",
50	                "0",
51	            ],
52	            capture_output=True,
53	            text=True,
54	        )
55	        content = read_text(Path(report_path))
56	        if not content.strip():
57	            return []
58	        return json.loads(content)
59	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, FileNotFoundError):
60	        return []
61	    finally:
62	        Path(report_path).unlink(missing_ok=True)
63

65	def run_gitleaks_workdir(target_path: str) -> list[dict]:
66	    """Run gitleaks on working directory and return findings as JSON."""

98	def redact_secret(secret: str, keep_chars: int = 3) -> str:
99	    """Redact secret keeping first/last N chars: sk-abc...xyz"""
100	    if len(secret) <= keep_chars * 2 + 3:
101	        return "[REDACTED]"
102	    return f"{secret[:keep_chars]}...{secret[-keep_chars:]}"
103

105	def redact_file(file_path: Path, findings: list[dict]) -> bool:
106	    """Redact secrets in a file. Returns True if modified."""
107	    content = read_text(file_path)
108	    original = content
109	
110	    file_findings = [
111	        f for f in findings if Path(f["File"]).resolve() == file_path.resolve()
112	    ]
113	
114	    for finding in file_findings:
115	        secret = finding.get("Secret", "")
116	        if secret and secret in content:
117	            content = content.replace(secret, redact_secret(secret))
118	
119	    if content != original:
120	        write_text(file_path, content)
121	        return True
122	    return False

126	    """Filter findings to only include .specstory/history/ files."""

130	# Matches actual PEM private key blocks
131	_PEM_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(
132	    r"-----BEGIN[^-]*PRIV***KEY[^-]*-----.*?-----END[^-]*PRIV***KEY[^-]*-----",
133	    re.DOTALL,
134	)
135	
136	# Matches the literal string the detect-private-key hook greps for
137	_PRIVATE_KEY_STR = "PRIV***KEY"
138	
139	
140	def find_private_key_files(files: list[Path]) -> dict[Path, list[str]]:
141	    """Find files containing private key patterns. Returns {path: [match_descriptions]}."""
142	    results: dict[Path, list[str]] = {}
143	    for path in files:
144	        if not path.is_file() or path.suffix != ".md":
145	            continue
146	        try:
147	            content = read_text(path)
148	        except OSError:
149	            continue
150	        if _PRIVATE_KEY_STR not in content:
151	            continue
152	        matches = []
153	        pem_blocks = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.findall(content)
154	        if pem_blocks:
155	            matches.append(f"{len(pem_blocks)} PEM private key block(s)")
156	        # Count remaining mentions (outside PEM blocks)
157	        without_pem = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.sub("", content)
158	        mention_count = without_pem.count(_PRIVATE_KEY_STR)
159	        if mention_count:
160	            matches.append(f'{mention_count} "{_PRIVATE_KEY_STR}" mention(s)')
161	        if matches:
162	            results[path] = matches
163	    return results

166	def redact_private_keys(file_path: Path) -> bool:
167	    """Redact private key patterns in a file. Returns True if modified."""
168	    content = read_text(file_path)
169	    original = content
170	    # Replace full PEM blocks
171	    content = _PEM_BLOCK_RE.sub("[REDACTED PRIV***KEY BLOCK]", content)
172	    # Replace remaining literal "PRIV***KEY" mentions
173	    content = content.replace(_PRIVATE_KEY_STR, "PRIV***KEY")
174	    if content != original:
175	        write_text(file_path, content)
176	        return True
177	    return False

228	            print()
229	    else:

232	    # --- Detect private key patterns ---
233	    if args.working_dir:
234	        scan_files = list(specstory_path.glob("*.md"))
235	    else:

240	            text=True,
241	        )

244	            for f in result.stdout.strip().splitlines()
245	            if f.startswith(".specstory/history/") and f.endswith(".md")
246	        ]
247

249	    if pk_files:
250	        has_issues = True
251	        print(f"Found private key pattern(s) in {len(pk_files)} file(s):\n")
252	        for path, descriptions in pk_files.items():

279

282	            [Path(f) for f in modified_files if Path(f).is_file()]
283	        )
284	        if remaining_pk:

286	            return 1

289	        print("Review changes with: git diff")

291	        return 0

```text
1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
11	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
12	
13	## Architecture
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart TB
17	    subgraph Bootstrap["1. Bootstrap"]
18	        BREW[Homebrew macOS]
19	        UV[uv] --> ANS[ansible]
20	        MISE[mise]
21	    end
22	
23	    subgraph Chezmoi["2. chezmoi apply"]
24	        DOT[Config files<br/>~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/]
25	        ANSDIR[~/.ansible/]
26	        BREWFILE[Brewfiles<br/>~/.config/homebrew/]
27	    end
28	
29	    subgraph Ansible["3. Ansible Playbooks"]
30	        BASE[base]
31	        ZSH[zsh]
32	        NVIM[neovim]
33	        DEVTOOLS[devtools]
34	        UVTOOLS[python_uv_tools]
35	        CARGO[rust_cargo_tools]
36	        LLMTOOLS[llm_tools]
37	    end
38	
39	    subgraph BrewBundle["4. Brew Bundle opt-in"]
40	        CASKS[GUI Apps]
41	        MAS[App Store]
42	    end
43	
44	    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible
45	    Chezmoi -.-> BrewBundle
46	    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM
47	    MISE -.->|Rust| CARGO
48	    UV -.->|Python tools| UVTOOLS
49	    UV -.->|LiteLLM| LLMTOOLS
50	    BREW -.->|casks| CASKS
51	    BREW -.->|formulae / casks| LLMTOOLS
52	```
53	
54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	```bash
57	# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
58	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
59	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
60	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
61	
62	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
63	#   chezmoi cd
64	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
65	#   exit
66	```
67	
68	This automatically:
69	
70	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
71	2. Deploys all config files
72	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
73	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled)
74	
75	### After install
76	
77	- `~/.local/bin` is auto-appended to `~/.bashrc` so `chezmoi`, `uv`, and `mise` stay reachable from bash.
78	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible `zsh` role switches your login shell to zsh automatically. Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` now.
79	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER`.
80	- Open a new shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) after install so PATH changes take effect.
81	
82	### Optional Components
83	
84	During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
85	
86	| Option | Default | Description |
87	|--------|---------|-------------|
88	| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, RTK, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
89	| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
90	| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.) |
91	| `installLlmTools` | false | Local LLM tools: Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit, models |
92	| `installAiDesktopApps` | false | macOS AI desktop apps via Homebrew Brewfile (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenCode Desktop, Antigravity, Codex Desktop on Apple Silicon; `ollama-app` also requires `installLlmTools=true`) |
93	| `installBrewApps` | false | General GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (terminals, browsers, utilities, mas; excludes AI desktop apps) |
94	| `installInputMethod` | false | Traditional Chinese input methods (McBopomofo, RIME/Squirrel on macOS; ibus-rime on Linux) |
95	| `installNetworkingTools` | false | Networking CLI tools (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, rustscan, etc.) |
96	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
97	
98	To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
99	
100	## What You Get
```

```text
- name: Install bats-core from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
    - bats_recheck.rc != 0
  block:
    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (bats)
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Get latest bats-core release
      ansible.builtin.uri:
        url: https://api.github.com/repos/bats-core/bats-core/releases/latest
        return_content: true
      register: bats_release

    - name: Download bats-core tarball
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: "https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/archive/refs/tags/{{ bats_release.json.tag_name }}.tar.gz"
        dest: /tmp/bats.tar.gz
        mode: '0644'
        timeout: 120
      retries: 3
      delay: 5

    - name: Extract and install bats-core to ~/.local
      ansible.builtin.shell: |
        set -euo pipefail
        rm -rf /tmp/bats-extract
        mkdir -p /tmp/bats-extract
        tar -xzf /tmp/bats.tar.gz -C /tmp/bats-extract --strip-components=1
        /tmp/bats-extract/install.sh "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local"
      args:
        executable: /bin/bash
      changed_when: true

    - name: Clean up bats temp files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ item }}"
        state: absent
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ssh-to-bitwarden - Import SSH key pairs into Bitwarden vault
3	#
4	# Scans a directory (default: ~/.ssh) for SSH private keys, shows an
5	# interactive menu for selecting which keys to import, then creates
6	# Bitwarden vault items for each selected key.
7	#
8	# Requirements: bw (Bitwarden CLI >= 2024.x), jq, ssh-keygen
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   ssh-to-bitwarden [OPTIONS]
12	#
13	# Options:
14	#   -d, --dir DIR       Directory to scan (default: ~/.ssh)
15	#   -a, --all           Import all discovered keys without prompting
16	#   -n, --dry-run       Show what would be imported without creating items
17	#   -p, --prefix STR    Prefix for Bitwarden item names (default: "SSH")
18	#   -h, --help          Show this help message
19	
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	# ── Defaults ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
23	SSH_DIR="$HOME/.ssh"
24	IMPORT_ALL=false
25	DRY_RUN=false
26	NAME_PREFIX="SSH"
27	
28	# Field separator for internal record passing (ASCII Unit Separator)
29	FS=$'\x1f'
30	
31	# ── Colors (disabled if not a terminal) ───────────────────────────────
32	if [ -t 1 ]; then
33	  BOLD='\033[1m'    DIM='\033[2m'    RESET='\033[0m'
34	  GREEN='\033[32m'  YELLOW='\033[33m' RED='\033[31m' CYAN='\033[36m'
35	else
36	  BOLD='' DIM='' RESET='' GREEN='' YELLOW='' RED='' CYAN=''
37	fi
38	
39	# ── Helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
40	info()  { printf "${CYAN}[INFO]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
41	ok()    { printf "${GREEN}[OK]${RESET}    %s\n" "$*"; }
42	warn()  { printf "${YELLOW}[WARN]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
43	error() { printf "${RED}[ERROR]${RESET} %s\n" "$*" >&2; }
44	skip()  { printf "${DIM}[SKIP]${RESET}  %s\n" "$*"; }
45	
46	usage() {
47	  cat <<'USAGE'
48	ssh-to-bitwarden - Import SSH key pairs into Bitwarden vault
49	
50	Usage:
51	  ssh-to-bitwarden [OPTIONS]
52	
53	Options:
54	  -d, --dir DIR       Directory to scan (default: ~/.ssh)
55	  -a, --all           Import all discovered keys without prompting
56	  -n, --dry-run       Show what would be imported without creating items
57	  -p, --prefix STR    Prefix for Bitwarden item names (default: "SSH")
58	  -h, --help          Show this help message
59	
60	Examples:
61	  ssh-to-bitwarden                  # Interactive mode, scan ~/.ssh
62	  ssh-to-bitwarden --all            # Import all keys without prompting
63	  ssh-to-bitwarden -d /tmp/keys     # Scan a custom directory
64	  ssh-to-bitwarden --dry-run        # Preview what would be imported
65	USAGE
66	  exit 0
67	}
68	
69	# ── Parse arguments ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
70	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
71	  case "$1" in
72	    -d|--dir)     SSH_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	    -a|--all)     IMPORT_ALL=true; shift ;;
74	    -n|--dry-run) DRY_RUN=true; shift ;;
75	    -p|--prefix)  NAME_PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	    -h|--help)    usage ;;
77	    *)            error "Unknown option: $1"; usage ;;
78	  esac
79	done
80	
81	# ── Dependency checks ────────────────────────────────────────────────
82	for cmd in bw jq ssh-keygen; do
83	  if ! command -v "$cmd" &>/dev/null; then
84	    error "Required command '$cmd' not found. Please install it first."
85	    exit 1
86	  fi
87	done
88	
89	# ── Discover SSH private keys ────────────────────────────────────────
90	# Scans the given directory for files that look like SSH private keys.
91	# Outputs one file path per line.
92	discover_keys() {
93	  local dir="$1"
94	
95	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
96	    error "Directory not found: $dir"
97	    exit 1
98	  fi
99	
100	  while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
101	    local name
102	    name=$(basename "$file")
103	
104	    # Skip known non-key files
105	    case "$name" in
106	      *.pub|known_hosts*|config|authorized_keys*|*.swp|*.swo|*~|*.un~|*.log) continue ;;
107	    esac
108	
109	    # Check if file begins with a PEM private key header
110	    if head -1 "$file" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^\-\-\-\-\-BEGIN.*PRIV***KEY\-\-\-\-\-'; then
111	      echo "$file"
112	    fi
113	  done < <(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
114	}
115	
116	# ── Extract key metadata ─────────────────────────────────────────────
117	# Returns a FS-delimited record:
118	#   privkey FS pubkey FS fingerprint FS key_type FS basename
119	get_key_info() {
120	  local privkey="$1"
121	  local pubkey="${privkey}.pub"
122	  local name
123	  name=$(basename "$privkey")
124	
125	  local fingerprint="N/A"
126	  local key_type="unknown"
127	
128	  # Look for a matching .pub file
129	  if [ ! -f "$pubkey" ]; then
130	    local stem="${privkey%.*}"
131	    if [ -f "${stem}.pub" ]; then
132	      pubkey="${stem}.pub"
133	    else
134	      pubkey=""
135	    fi
136	  fi
137	
138	  # Extract fingerprint and type from ssh-keygen
139	  # Output format: "bits SHA256:xxx comment (TYPE)"
140	  local keygen_src="${pubkey:-$privkey}"
141	  local keygen_output
142	  keygen_output=$(ssh-keygen -lf "$keygen_src" 2>/dev/null) || true
143	
144	  if [ -n "$keygen_output" ]; then
145	    fingerprint=$(awk '{print $2}' <<< "$keygen_output")
146	    key_type=$(grep -oE '\([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\)\s*$' <<< "$keygen_output" | tr -d '() ') || key_type="unknown"
147	    [ -z "$key_type" ] && key_type="unknown"
148	  fi
149	
150	  printf '%s' "${privkey}${FS}${pubkey}${FS}${fingerprint}${FS}${key_type}${FS}${name}"
151	}
152	
153	# Parse a key-info record into variables.
154	# Usage: parse_key_info "$record"  (sets: K_PRIV, K_PUB, K_FP, K_TYPE, K_NAME)
155	parse_key_info() {
156	  local record="$1"
157	  IFS="$FS" read -r K_PRIV K_PUB K_FP K_TYPE K_NAME <<< "$record"
158	}
159	
160	# ── Display key table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
161	display_keys() {
162	  local -n _keys=$1
163	  local count=${#_keys[@]}
164	
165	  printf "\n${BOLD}Found %d SSH private key(s) in %s:${RESET}\n\n" "$count" "$SSH_DIR"
166	  printf "  ${BOLD}%-4s  %-28s  %-10s  %-10s  %-50s${RESET}\n" "#" "Name" "Type" "Has .pub" "Fingerprint"
167	  printf "  %-4s  %-28s  %-10s  %-10s  %-50s\n" "----" "----------------------------" "----------" "----------" "--------------------------------------------------"
168	
169	  local i=1
170	  for record in "${_keys[@]}"; do
171	    parse_key_info "$record"
172	    local has_pub="no"
173	    [ -n "$K_PUB" ] && [ -f "$K_PUB" ] && has_pub="yes"
174	    printf "  ${CYAN}%-4s${RESET}  %-28s  %-10s  %-10s  %s\n" \
175	      "$i" "$K_NAME" "$K_TYPE" "$has_pub" "$K_FP"
176	    ((i++))
177	  done
178	  echo ""
179	}
180	
181	# ── Interactive selection ─────────────────────────────────────────────
182	select_keys() {
183	  local -n _keys=$1
184	  local -n _selected=$2
185	  local count=${#_keys[@]}
186	
187	  while true; do
188	    printf "${BOLD}Select keys to import:${RESET}\n"
189	    printf "  ${DIM}Enter numbers separated by spaces (e.g. 1 3 4)${RESET}\n"
190	    printf "  ${DIM}Enter 'a' for all, 'q' to quit, 'l' to list again${RESET}\n"
191	    printf "> "
192	    read -r choice
193	
194	    case "$choice" in
195	      q|Q)
196	        echo "Aborted."
197	        exit 0
198	        ;;
199	      a|A)
200	        _selected=("${_keys[@]}")
201	        return 0
202	        ;;
203	      l|L)
204	        display_keys _keys
205	        continue
206	        ;;
207	      "")
208	        warn "No selection made. Try again."
209	        continue
210	        ;;
211	    esac
212	
213	    # Parse numeric selections
214	    _selected=()
215	    local valid=true
216	    for num in $choice; do
217	      if ! [[ "$num" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [ "$num" -lt 1 ] || [ "$num" -gt "$count" ]; then
218	        error "Invalid selection: $num (must be 1-$count)"
219	        valid=false
220	        break
221	      fi
222	      _selected+=("${_keys[$((num - 1))]}")
223	    done
224	
225	    if $valid && [ ${#_selected[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
226	      return 0
227	    fi
228	  done
229	}
230	
231	# ── Check for existing items in vault ─────────────────────────────────
232	check_existing() {
233	  local name="$1"
234	  local existing
235	  existing=$(bw list items --search "$name" 2>/dev/null \
236	    | jq -r --arg n "$name" '.[] | select(.name == $n) | .id' 2>/dev/null) || true
237	  echo "$existing"
238	}
239	
240	# ── Import a single key ──────────────────────────────────────────────
241	import_key() {
242	  parse_key_info "$1"
243	
244	  local item_name="${NAME_PREFIX}: ${K_NAME}"
245	  local has_pub=false
246	  [ -n "$K_PUB" ] && [ -f "$K_PUB" ] && has_pub=true
247	
248	  info "Importing: ${K_NAME}"
249	  printf "       Type: %s | Fingerprint: %s | Has .pub: %s\n" \
250	    "$K_TYPE" "$K_FP" "$has_pub"
251	
252	  # Check for duplicates
253	  local existing_id
254	  existing_id=$(check_existing "$item_name")
255	  if [ -n "$existing_id" ]; then
256	    warn "Item '$item_name' already exists in vault (id: $existing_id)"
257	    if ! $IMPORT_ALL; then
258	      printf "       Overwrite? [y/N] > "
259	      read -r overwrite
260	      if [[ ! "$overwrite" =~ ^[yY]$ ]]; then
261	        skip "Skipped $K_NAME (already exists)"
262	        echo ""
263	        return 0
264	      fi
265	      # Delete old item before re-creating
266	      info "Deleting existing item $existing_id..."
267	      bw delete item "$existing_id" >/dev/null
268	    else
269	      skip "Skipped $K_NAME (already exists; use interactive mode to overwrite)"
270	      echo ""
271	      return 0
272	    fi
273	  fi
274	
275	  if $DRY_RUN; then
276	    ok "[DRY RUN] Would create: $item_name"
277	    echo ""
278	    return 0
279	  fi
280	
281	  local private_key_content
282	  private_key_content=$(cat "$K_PRIV")
283	
284	  local public_key_content=""
285	  if $has_pub; then
286	    public_key_content=$(cat "$K_PUB")
287	  fi
288	
289	  # Build vault item JSON
290	  local item_json result item_id
291	
292	  if [ "$K_FP" != "N/A" ]; then
293	    # SSH Key item (type 5)
294	    item_json=$(jq -n \
295	      --arg name "$item_name" \
296	      --arg priv "$private_key_content" \
297	      --arg pub "$public_key_content" \
298	      --arg fp "$K_FP" \
299	      '{
300	        type: 5,
301	        name: $name,
302	        sshKey: {
303	          privateKey: $priv,
304	          publicKey: $pub,
305	          keyFingerprint: $fp
306	        }
307	      }')
308	  else
309	    # Fallback: Secure Note (type 2)
310	    warn "Cannot extract fingerprint; storing as Secure Note instead"
311	    item_json=$(jq -n \
312	      --arg name "$item_name" \
313	      --arg notes "$private_key_content" \
314	      '{
315	        type: 2,
316	        name: $name,
317	        notes: $notes,
318	        secureNote: { type: 0 }
319	      }')
320	  fi
321	
322	  result=$(echo "$item_json" | bw encode | bw create item)
323	  item_id=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.id')
324	  ok "Created: $item_name (id: $item_id)"
325	  echo ""
326	}
327	
328	# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
329	main() {
330	  echo ""
331	  printf "${BOLD}ssh-to-bitwarden${RESET} - Import SSH keys into Bitwarden vault\n"
332	  echo ""
333	
334	  if $DRY_RUN; then
335	    warn "Dry-run mode enabled. No items will be created."
336	    echo ""
337	  fi
338	
339	  # Discover keys
340	  info "Scanning $SSH_DIR for SSH private keys..."
341	  local key_files=()
342	  while IFS= read -r line; do
343	    [ -z "$line" ] && continue
344	    key_files+=("$line")
345	  done < <(discover_keys "$SSH_DIR")
346	
347	  if [ ${#key_files[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
348	    warn "No SSH private keys found in $SSH_DIR"
349	    exit 0
350	  fi
351	
352	  # Gather metadata for each key
353	  local key_infos=()
354	  for keyfile in "${key_files[@]}"; do
355	    key_infos+=("$(get_key_info "$keyfile")")
356	  done
357	
358	  # Sort by name for consistent display
359	  IFS=$'\n' key_infos=($(for r in "${key_infos[@]}"; do echo "$r"; done | sort -t"$FS" -k5))
360	  unset IFS
361	
362	  # Display discovered keys
363	  display_keys key_infos
364	
365	  # Select keys to import
366	  local selected=()
367	  if $IMPORT_ALL; then
368	    info "Importing all keys (--all flag)"
369	    selected=("${key_infos[@]}")
370	  else
371	    select_keys key_infos selected
372	  fi
373	
374	  local total=${#selected[@]}
375	  printf "\n${BOLD}Importing %d key(s)...${RESET}\n\n" "$total"
376	
377	  # Ensure vault is unlocked (unless dry-run)
378	  if ! $DRY_RUN; then
379	    local status
380	    status=$(bw status 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.status')
381	    case "$status" in
382	      unauthenticated)
383	        error "Not logged in. Run 'bw login' first."
384	        exit 1
385	        ;;
386	      locked)
387	        info "Vault is locked. Unlocking..."
388	        BW_SESSION=$(bw unlock --raw)
389	        export BW_SESSION
390	        ok "Vault unlocked."
391	        ;;
392	      unlocked)
393	        ok "Vault already unlocked."
394	        ;;
395	    esac
396	
397	    info "Syncing vault..."
398	    bw sync >/dev/null
399	    ok "Vault synced."
400	    echo ""
401	  fi
402	
403	  # Import each selected key
404	  local imported=0 failed=0
405	  for record in "${selected[@]}"; do
406	    if import_key "$record"; then
407	      ((imported++))
408	    else
409	      ((failed++))
410	    fi
411	  done
412	
413	  # Summary
414	  echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
415	  if $DRY_RUN; then
416	    printf "${BOLD}Dry run complete.${RESET} %d key(s) would be imported.\n" "$total"
417	  else
418	    printf "${BOLD}Done!${RESET} %d key(s) processed" "$total"
419	    [ "$failed" -gt 0 ] && printf " (%d failed)" "$failed"
420	    printf ".\n"
421	  fi
422	  echo ""
423	  if ! $DRY_RUN; then
424	    printf "${DIM}Verify with: bw list items --search '%s'${RESET}\n" "$NAME_PREFIX"
425	  fi
426	}
427	
428	main
429

```text
1	# Add bats-core to devtools role
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Add [bats-core](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core) — the standard Bash testing framework — as a devtool across all supported platforms. Bats is pure-bash, portable, and arch-agnostic (so no `armv7l` skip logic needed). This mirrors how other shell-adjacent tools are installed in the `devtools` role and makes `bats` available for testing shell scripts in this repo and beyond.
6	
7	Scope intentionally excludes `bats-support` / `bats-assert` / `bats-file` helper libraries — those are project-local (vendored per-repo as submodules), not system-wide.
8	
9	## Install strategy
10	
11	| Platform | Method | Notes |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| macOS | Homebrew formula `bats-core` | Append to existing `homebrew` task list |
14	| Linux (sudo) | `apt install bats` | Ubuntu 20.04+ has a `bats` package |
15	| Linux (noRoot) | GitHub release tarball + `./install.sh ~/.local` | Pure-bash, no arch matrix needed |
16	
17	The GitHub-release fallback uses the official `install.sh` script inside the tarball, which places `bats` in `$PREFIX/bin` and libraries in `$PREFIX/lib/bats-core` / `$PREFIX/libexec/bats-core`. That matches how `~/.local` is already used across the role.
18	
19	## Files to modify
20	
21	### 1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`
22	
23	**Header comment (line 3)** — add `bats` to the tools list.
24	
25	**macOS block (line 15-43)** — insert `bats-core` into the alphabetical-ish list; place near `coreutils`/`taplo` or at end of list:
26	```yaml
27	- bats-core
28	```
29	
30	**Linux block** — add a new `# --- bats ---` section. Follow the exact pattern used by `bat` (lines 337-421): short apt install (with `tags: [sudo]` and `become: true`), followed by a user-level fallback that checks `command -v bats` and falls back to the GitHub tarball. Skeleton:
31	
32	```yaml
33	# --- bats ---
34	- name: Install bats (Debian/Ubuntu)
35	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
36	  become: true
37	  tags: [sudo]
38	  ansible.builtin.apt:
39	    name: bats
40	    state: present
41	
42	# --- bats (user-level fallback) ---
43	- name: Re-check if bats is installed
44	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
45	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v bats
46	  register: bats_recheck
47	  changed_when: false
48	  failed_when: false
49	  environment:
50	    PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
51	
52	- name: Install bats-core from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
53	  when:
54	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
55	    - bats_recheck.rc != 0
56	  block:
57	    - name: Ensure ~/.local/bin exists (bats)
58	      ansible.builtin.file:
59	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin"
60	        state: directory
61	        mode: '0755'
62	
63	    - name: Get latest bats-core release
64	      ansible.builtin.uri:
65	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/bats-core/bats-core/releases/latest
66	        return_content: true
67	      register: bats_release
68	
69	    - name: Download bats-core tarball
70	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
71	        url: "https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/archive/refs/tags/{{ bats_release.json.tag_name }}.tar.gz"
72	        dest: /tmp/bats.tar.gz
73	        mode: '0644'
74	        timeout: 120
75	      retries: 3
76	      delay: 5
77	
78	    - name: Extract and install bats-core to ~/.local
79	      ansible.builtin.shell: |
80	        set -euo pipefail
81	        rm -rf /tmp/bats-extract
82	        mkdir -p /tmp/bats-extract
83	        tar -xzf /tmp/bats.tar.gz -C /tmp/bats-extract --strip-components=1
84	        /tmp/bats-extract/install.sh "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local"
85	      args:
86	        executable: /bin/bash
87	      changed_when: true
88	
89	    - name: Clean up bats temp files
90	      ansible.builtin.file:
91	        path: "{{ item }}"
92	        state: absent
93	      loop:
94	        - /tmp/bats.tar.gz
95	        - /tmp/bats-extract
96	
97	  rescue:
98	    - name: Warn bats-core installation failed
99	      ansible.builtin.debug:
100	        msg: "bats-core installation failed (likely network timeout) - skipping"
101	
102	    - name: Clean up bats temp files after failure
103	      ansible.builtin.file:
104	        path: "{{ item }}"
105	        state: absent
106	      loop:
107	        - /tmp/bats.tar.gz
108	        - /tmp/bats-extract
109	```

65	# --- Proxy helpers (generic) ---
66	# Portable proxy management: honor $LOCAL_PROXY_URL, else auto-probe common
67	# loopback ports (Clash 7890/7891, ClashX 1087, Privoxy 8118, generic 8080).
68	# Detection result is cached per-shell in _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE; use
69	# `proxy-refresh` after starting/stopping the proxy.
70	#
71	# Environment variables honored:
72	#   LOCAL_PROXY_URL         HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890).
73	#                           If unset, ports are auto-probed.
74	#   LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL   Optional separate SOCKS5 endpoint (e.g.
75	#                           socks5://127.0.0.1:7891). Used for ALL_PROXY /
76	#                           all_proxy when set; otherwise these fall back to
77	#                           LOCAL_PROXY_URL / the probe result. Useful when
78	#                           Clash is configured with split `port:` and
79	#                           `socks-port:` instead of `mixed-port:`.
80	#   LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1  Run `proxy-on` silently at shell startup
81	#                           whenever a proxy is detected. Handy on machines
82	#                           that always route through the local proxy.
83	
84	: "${_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE:=}"
85	__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS=(7890 7891 1087 8118 8080)
86	
87	__zsh_net_detect_proxy() {
88	  [[ -n "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]] && return 0
89	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" ]]; then
90	    _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="$LOCAL_PROXY_URL"
91	    return 0
92	  fi
93	  local port
94	  for port in "${__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[@]}"; do
95	    if nc -z -w1 127.0.0.1 "$port" 2>/dev/null; then
96	      _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="http://127.0.0.1:$port"
97	      return 0
98	    fi
99	  done
100	  _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE="none"
101	  return 1
102	}
103	
104	# Resolve the URL that should be used for ALL_PROXY / all_proxy.
105	# Falls back to the HTTP proxy when no SOCKS-specific URL is set (works for
106	# mixed-port Clash configs where one port serves both HTTP and SOCKS).
107	__zsh_net_all_proxy_url() {
108	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]]; then
109	    print -r -- "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL"
110	  else
111	    print -r -- "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE"
112	  fi
113	}
114	
115	# Run one command with proxy env applied to the child process only.
116	withproxy() {
117	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
118	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
119	    "$@"
120	    return
121	  fi
122	  local all_url
123	  all_url="$(__zsh_net_all_proxy_url)"
124	  http_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
125	  https_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
126	  HTTP_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
127	  HTTPS_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
128	  ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
129	  all_proxy="$all_url" \
130	    "$@"
131	}
132	
133	# Run direct first; on non-zero exit, retry via proxy if one is available.
134	try_direct_then_proxy() {
135	  "$@" && return 0
136	  local rc=$?
137	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
138	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
139	    return $rc
140	  fi
141	  print -u2 "[retry via proxy $_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE]"
142	  withproxy "$@"
143	}
144	
145	# Export proxy env vars to the current shell (all downstream commands inherit).
146	# If $1 is "-q", suppress the success message (used by auto-activate).
147	proxy-on() {
148	  local quiet=0
149	  [[ "$1" == "-q" ]] && quiet=1
150	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
151	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
152	    (( quiet )) || print -u2 "proxy-on: no proxy detected (set \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL or start your proxy, then \`proxy-refresh\`)"
153	    return 1
154	  fi
155	  local all_url
156	  all_url="$(__zsh_net_all_proxy_url)"
157	  export http_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
158	         https_proxy="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
159	         HTTP_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
160	         HTTPS_PROXY="$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" \
161	         ALL_PROXY="$all_url" \
162	         all_proxy="$all_url"
163	  if (( ! quiet )); then
164	    if [[ "$all_url" == "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" ]]; then
165	      print "proxy ON  ->  $_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE"
166	    else
167	      print "proxy ON  ->  http/https=$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE  all/socks=$all_url"
168	    fi
169	  fi
170	}
171	
172	# Unset all proxy env vars from the current shell.
173	proxy-off() {
174	  unset http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy
175	  print "proxy OFF"
176	}
177	
178	# Report current proxy state: active / available / unavailable.
179	proxy-status() {
180	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
181	  local shell_active=""
182	  if [[ -n "$http_proxy$https_proxy$ALL_PROXY" ]]; then
183	    shell_active="yes"
184	  fi
185	  local source="probe"
186	  [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_URL" ]] && source="LOCAL_PROXY_URL env"
187	
188	  if [[ "$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE" == "none" ]]; then
189	    print "proxy: unavailable (no \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL; no loopback port from ${__ZSH_NET_PROXY_PROBE_PORTS[*]} reachable)"
190	    [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && print "  note: shell env still has proxy vars set -- run \`proxy-off\` to clear"
191	    return 1
192	  fi
193	
194	  local state="available"
195	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && state="active   "
196	  local hint="(not exported; use \`withproxy\`, \`try_direct_then_proxy\`, or \`proxy-on\`)"
197	  [[ -n "$shell_active" ]] && hint="(exported in current shell)"
198	
199	  print "proxy: $state http=$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE  source=$source  $hint"
200	  if [[ -n "$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL" ]]; then
201	    print "  socks=$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL  source=LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL env"
202	  fi
203	}
204	
205	# Clear the cached detection and re-probe; call after toggling your proxy.
206	proxy-refresh() {
207	  _ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE=""
208	  __zsh_net_detect_proxy
209	  proxy-status
210	}
211	
212	# Optional auto-activation: when $LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1 is set before
213	# this file is sourced, silently call `proxy-on` if a proxy is detected.
214	# Set the env var in a machine-local zsh file (or ~/.zshenv) on machines that
215	# should always route through the loopback proxy.
216	if [[ "$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE" == "1" ]]; then
217	  proxy-on -q
218	fi
