# Lightweight shell testing for dotfiles (bats + shellcheck + shfmt)

## Context

This is a personal dotfiles repo. Bats is already installed via the `devtools` ansible role (previous plan: `.claude/plans/bats-snuggly-volcano.md`), but nothing in the repo actually uses it — the sole "test" today is `docker-compose.yml` running ~30 inline bash assertions on tool/config presence.

Goals for this pass, per the user's scope decision:

- **Protect against painful regressions only** — proxy helpers in `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` are the one piece of pure logic that is used daily, silent when broken, and non-trivial (env precedence + port probing + SOCKS split).
- **Lint cheaply** — shellcheck + shfmt on commit catch a whole class of bugs per-bug more cheaply than writing tests.
- **Keep ceremony minimal** — no vendored `bats-assert`/`bats-file`/`bats-support` submodules; no CI; no fixture frameworks; no refactors of shell code purely for testability.

What's explicitly **not** in scope: git-helper unit tests (`gundo`/`gcam-amend`), Python redact-script tests, ansible-role testing, bootstrap-script testing, chezmoi-template expansion tests, GitHub Actions CI.

## Files to add

### 1. `tests/test_helper.bash`

Tiny shared helper. Sourced by every `.bats` file. Provides:

- `REPO_ROOT` pointing at the chezmoi source dir (derived from `BATS_TEST_DIRNAME`).
- `setup_path_stub()` — creates a temp dir, prepends to `PATH`, returns path so individual tests can drop fake binaries (e.g. a fake `nc`).
- `teardown` hook clears any temp dirs registered via `_BATS_STUBS`.

Keep it under ~40 lines. No external libraries.

### 2. `tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`

1	# dotfiles
2	
3	Cross-platform development environment setup using **chezmoi** + **ansible**.
4	
5	- **chezmoi**: manages config files (dotfiles)
6	- **ansible**: installs system dependencies and tools
7	
8	## Prerequisites
9	
10	- [chezmoi](https://www.chezmoi.io/install/)
11	- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (for ansible)
12	
13	## Architecture
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart TB
17	    subgraph Bootstrap["1. Bootstrap"]
18	        BREW[Homebrew macOS]
19	        UV[uv] --> ANS[ansible]
20	        MISE[mise]
21	    end
22	
23	    subgraph Chezmoi["2. chezmoi apply"]
24	        DOT[Config files<br/>~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/]
25	        ANSDIR[~/.ansible/]
26	        BREWFILE[Brewfiles<br/>~/.config/homebrew/]
27	    end
28	
29	    subgraph Ansible["3. Ansible Playbooks"]
30	        BASE[base]
31	        ZSH[zsh]
32	        NVIM[neovim]
33	        DEVTOOLS[devtools]
34	        UVTOOLS[python_uv_tools]
35	        CARGO[rust_cargo_tools]
36	        LLMTOOLS[llm_tools]
37	    end
38	
39	    subgraph BrewBundle["4. Brew Bundle opt-in"]
40	        CASKS[GUI Apps]
41	        MAS[App Store]
42	    end
43	
44	    Bootstrap --> Chezmoi --> Ansible
45	    Chezmoi -.-> BrewBundle
46	    MISE -.->|Node.js, Rust| NVIM
47	    MISE -.->|Rust| CARGO
48	    UV -.->|Python tools| UVTOOLS
49	    UV -.->|LiteLLM| LLMTOOLS
50	    BREW -.->|casks| CASKS
51	    BREW -.->|formulae / casks| LLMTOOLS
52	```
53	
54	## Quick Setup
55	
56	```bash
57	# One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
58	# Uses HTTPS to avoid SSH key setup on fresh machines.
59	export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
60	sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply "https://github.com/$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git"
61	
62	# After install, switch the chezmoi source repo to SSH (so future `chezmoi update` uses your SSH key):
63	#   chezmoi cd
64	#   git remote set-url origin git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
65	#   exit
66	```
67	
68	This automatically:
69	
70	1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
71	2. Deploys all config files
72	3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
73	4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` is enabled, or on macOS if `installAiDesktopApps` is enabled)
74	
75	### After install
76	
77	- `~/.local/bin` is auto-appended to `~/.bashrc` so `chezmoi`, `uv`, and `mise` stay reachable from bash.
78	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible `zsh` role switches your login shell to zsh automatically. Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` now.
79	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER`.
80	- Open a new shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) after install so PATH changes take effect.
81	
82	### Optional Components
83	
84	During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
85	
86	| Option | Default | Description |
87	|--------|---------|-------------|
88	| `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, RTK, td, sidecar, specify-cli, etc. |
89	| `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
90	| `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, sqlit-tui, tmuxp, etc.) |
91	| `installLlmTools` | false | Local LLM tools: Ollama, LiteLLM, llmfit, models |
92	| `installAiDesktopApps` | false | macOS AI desktop apps via Homebrew Brewfile (Claude, ChatGPT, OpenCode Desktop, Antigravity, Codex Desktop on Apple Silicon; `ollama-app` also requires `installLlmTools=true`) |
93	| `installBrewApps` | false | General GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (terminals, browsers, utilities, mas; excludes AI desktop apps) |
94	| `installInputMethod` | false | Traditional Chinese input methods (McBopomofo, RIME/Squirrel on macOS; ibus-rime on Linux) |
95	| `installNetworkingTools` | false | Networking CLI tools (nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy, bandwhich, rustscan, etc.) |
96	| `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
97	
98	To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
99

101	
102	### Config Files

# Shared helpers for bats tests. Source from each .bats file:
#   load "../test_helper.bash"   # or the equivalent relative path
#
# Keep this file tiny. No bats-assert / bats-file / bats-support — plain
# bats built-ins ([ ], run, $status, $output) are enough.

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/.." && pwd)"
if [ "$(basename "$REPO_ROOT")" = "tests" ]; then
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT/.." && pwd)"
fi
export REPO_ROOT

_BATS_STUB_DIRS=()

setup_path_stub() {
  local dir
  dir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bats-stub.XXXXXX")"
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS+=("$dir")
  PATH="$dir:$PATH"
  export PATH
  printf '%s\n' "$dir"
}

teardown() {
  local dir
  for dir in "${_BATS_STUB_DIRS[@]:-}"; do
    [ -n "$dir" ] && [ -d "$dir" ] && rm -rf "$dir"
  done
  _BATS_STUB_DIRS=()
}

```

```bats
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Unit tests for dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh proxy helpers.
#
# Strategy: each test runs `zsh -f -c '...'` (no startup files) with the proxy
# file sourced fresh, so cache state ($_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE) can't leak between
# tests. `nc` is stubbed via a temp dir prepended to PATH so probes don't touch
# the network.

load "../test_helper.bash"

PROXY_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh"

# Helper: write a fake `nc` that exits 0 only when port matches $EXPECT_PORT
# (set by the calling test via env). All other ncs fail -> simulates closed.
_make_nc_stub() {
  local dir="$1"
  cat > "$dir/nc" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Walks args, takes last as port. matches $EXPECT_PORT.
port=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do port="$1"; shift; done
[ "$port" = "${EXPECT_PORT:-__none__}" ] && exit 0 || exit 1
STUB
  chmod +x "$dir/nc"
}

@test "detect_proxy: \$LOCAL_PROXY_URL is used verbatim, no probe" {
  result="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://sentinel:9999 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    __zsh_net_detect_proxy
    print -r -- \"\$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE\"
  ")"
  [ "$result" = "http://sentinel:9999" ]
}

@test "detect_proxy: probes default ports and picks first responder" {
  local stub
  stub="$(setup_path_stub)"
  _make_nc_stub "$stub"

  # Pick 1087 — third in the probe order (7890, 7891, 1087, 8118, 8080).
  # If probe order regressed or skipped a port, this would return a different URL.
  result="$(EXPECT_PORT=1087 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    __zsh_net_detect_proxy
    print -r -- \"\$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE\"
  ")"
  [ "$result" = "http://127.0.0.1:1087" ]
}

@test "detect_proxy: no responder sets cache=none and returns non-zero" {
  local stub
  stub="$(setup_path_stub)"
  # nc that always fails
  cat > "$stub/nc" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
exit 1
EOF
  chmod +x "$stub/nc"

  run zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    if __zsh_net_detect_proxy; then rc=0; else rc=\$?; fi
    print -r -- \"cache=\$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE rc=\$rc\"
  "
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"cache=none"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"rc=1"* ]]
}

@test "all_proxy_url: prefers LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL, falls back to cache" {
  # With SOCKS url set → returns SOCKS url.
  result="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://a:1 LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL=socks5://b:2 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    __zsh_net_detect_proxy
    __zsh_net_all_proxy_url
  ")"
  [ "$result" = "socks5://b:2" ]

  # Without SOCKS url → falls back to HTTP cache.
  result="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://a:1 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    __zsh_net_detect_proxy
    __zsh_net_all_proxy_url
  ")"
  [ "$result" = "http://a:1" ]
}

@test "proxy-on: exports all six proxy env vars" {
  output="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://test:1234 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    proxy-on -q
    for v in http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy; do
      printf '%s=%s\n' \"\$v\" \"\${(P)v}\"
    done
  ")"
  [[ "$output" == *"http_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"https_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"HTTP_PROXY=http://test:1234"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"HTTPS_PROXY=http://test:1234"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"ALL_PROXY=http://test:1234"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"all_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
}

@test "proxy-on: split HTTP/SOCKS wires http= and all= independently (fa4c063 guard)" {
  output="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://h:1 LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL=socks5://s:2 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    proxy-on -q
    printf 'http=%s\nhttps=%s\nall=%s\n' \"\$http_proxy\" \"\$https_proxy\" \"\$ALL_PROXY\"
  ")"
  [[ "$output" == *"http=http://h:1"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"https=http://h:1"* ]]
  [[ "$output" == *"all=socks5://s:2"* ]]
}

@test "proxy-off: clears all six proxy vars plus NO_PROXY / no_proxy" {
  output="$(LOCAL_PROXY_URL=http://x:1 zsh -f -c "
    source '$PROXY_FILE'
    proxy-on -q
    export NO_PROXY=localhost no_proxy=localhost
    proxy-off > /dev/null
    for v in http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy NO_PROXY no_proxy; do
      if [[ -n \"\${(P)v}\" ]]; then printf '%s=still-set\n' \"\$v\"; fi
    done
  ")"
  [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "proxy-status: returns 1 when unavailable, 0 when available" {
  local stub
  stub="$(setup_path_stub)"
  # nc always fails → no proxy detected
  cat > "$stub/nc" <<'EOF'

```bats
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Smoke tests intended to run inside the Docker `test` service container
# (see docker-compose.yml). They assert the post-`chezmoi apply` + post-ansible
# state of a fresh Ubuntu box.
#
# Do NOT run these on a host machine — they assume the chezmoi source lives at
# /tmp/dotfiles-source (matches Dockerfile COPY target) and that the container
# has just completed a full install.

load "../test_helper.bash"

SOURCE_DIR="${CHEZMOI_SOURCE_DIR:-/tmp/dotfiles-source}"

@test "chezmoi apply is idempotent (diff is empty after re-apply)" {
  # Re-apply should be a no-op. A non-empty diff means templates drift or
  # run_once state tracking is broken.
  run chezmoi apply
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  run chezmoi diff
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "zsh -n parses ~/.zshrc and ~/.zshenv without errors" {
  [ -f "$HOME/.zshrc" ]
  [ -f "$HOME/.zshenv" ]
  zsh -n "$HOME/.zshrc"
  zsh -n "$HOME/.zshenv"
}

@test "~/.config/zsh exists and every *.zsh file parses cleanly" {
  [ -d "$HOME/.config/zsh" ]
  # Parse every deployed zsh module. A regression here means a syntax error
  # slipped through into the interactive shell path.
  local file failures=0
  while IFS= read -r file; do
    if ! zsh -n "$file" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "zsh -n failed: $file" >&2
      failures=$((failures + 1))
    fi
  done < <(find "$HOME/.config/zsh" -type f -name '*.zsh')
  [ "$failures" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "neovim is installed and can run a headless lua call" {
  command -v nvim
  run nvim --headless "+lua print('ok')" +qa
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

@test "~/.config/nvim exists and init file is present" {
  [ -d "$HOME/.config/nvim" ]
  [ -f "$HOME/.config/nvim/init.lua" ] || [ -f "$HOME/.config/nvim/init.vim" ]
}

@test "core CLI tools are on PATH" {
  # These are the tools a user would notice missing. Not an exhaustive list.
  for cmd in nvim rg fd fzf zsh just bats; do
    command -v "$cmd" || {
      echo "missing on PATH: $cmd" >&2
      return 1
    }
  done
}

@test "oh-my-zsh plugins are installed" {
  local omz="$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins"
  [ -d "$omz/zsh-autosuggestions" ]
  [ -d "$omz/zsh-syntax-highlighting" ]
  [ -d "$omz/zsh-completions" ]
}

@test "unit tests pass in-container (zsh_proxy.bats under installed zsh)" {
  # Re-run the host unit tests inside the container. Catches regressions where
  # a zsh feature we rely on works on macOS but not on the Ubuntu-shipped zsh.
  [ -f "$SOURCE_DIR/tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats" ]
  run bats "$SOURCE_DIR/tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
}

```

# import_ssh_to_bw.sh

Import SSH key pairs into a Bitwarden vault using the `bw` CLI.

## Requirements

- `bw` (Bitwarden CLI >= 2024.x) -- provides the SSH Key item type (type 5)
- `jq` -- for building JSON payloads and parsing responses
- `ssh-keygen` -- for extracting fingerprints and key types

## How It Works

1. **Discovery** -- Scans `~/.ssh` (or a custom directory) for files starting with `-----BEGIN...PRIV***KEY-----`. Skips `.pub`, `known_hosts`, `config`, `authorized_keys`, swap files, etc.
2. **Metadata extraction** -- For each private key, looks for a matching `.pub` file (tries `<key>.pub` and `<stem>.pub`). Extracts the fingerprint, key type, and comment via `ssh-keygen -lf`.
3. **Interactive selection** -- Displays a table of discovered keys and prompts the user to pick which ones to import (by number, `a` for all, `q` to quit).
4. **Duplicate detection** -- Before creating an item, checks if an item with the same name already exists in the vault. In interactive mode, offers to overwrite; in `--all` mode, skips duplicates.
5. **Import** -- Creates a Bitwarden **SSH Key item** (type 5) with private key, public key, and fingerprint. Falls back to a **Secure Note** (type 2) if the fingerprint cannot be extracted.

## Usage


==> /Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/docs/tools/fzf.md <==

```md
# Shell Script Testing

How this repo tests shell code, the landscape of shell-testing tools, and when to reach for each.

---

## TL;DR for this repo

| Tool | Role | Scope |
|------|------|-------|
| [**bats-core**](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core) | Behaviour / unit tests | `tests/unit/`, `tests/smoke/` |
| [**shellcheck**](https://www.shellcheck.net/) | Static analysis (bugs, bad quoting) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` |
| [**shfmt**](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) | Formatter (consistency check) | Pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` |

Run everything with `just check-all`. Run just the fast unit suite with `just bats`. See [the repo tests/ tree](#how-this-repo-structures-tests) below.

**What's intentionally _not_ in scope:** ansible-role tests, bootstrap / `run_once` tests, chezmoi-template expansion tests, Python script tests, GitHub Actions CI. Coverage is deliberately narrow — this is a personal dotfiles repo, not a library.

---

## The three shell-testing frameworks

Most people pick between Bats, ZUnit, and ShellSpec. Short version of when each makes sense:

### Bats (Bash Automated Testing System) — what this repo uses

A Bash testing framework. Tests go in `*.bats` files; each test is a `@test "name" { ... }` block. Provides `run`, `$status`, `$output`, `setup`, `teardown`, plus TAP / JUnit output for CI.

Pick Bats when:

- You mainly write Bash.
- You're testing CLI scripts or zsh scripts via **black-box** behaviour (run the command, check exit code + stdout/stderr).
- You want the most popular / best-documented shell testing ecosystem.

Not ideal when:

- You're testing zsh-specific functions (plugins, autoload, `${(P)var}`, parameter expansion flags) at the function level — Bats has no zsh affinity.
- You need mocking, coverage, or BDD grammar.

Companion libraries (optional, **not vendored here** to keep ceremony low):

- [`bats-assert`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-assert) — `assert_equal`, `assert_output --partial`, etc.
- [`bats-file`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-file) — file-system assertions.
- [`bats-support`](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-support) — shared helpers for the above.

### ZUnit — zsh-native

A [ZSH testing framework](https://github.com/zunit-zsh/zunit). Testcase syntax is similar to Bats but written in zsh, so zsh-specific constructs work naturally in both the tests and the code under test.

Pick ZUnit when:

- You're writing a zsh plugin, autoload function, or zsh-heavy library.
- You want the test harness to _be_ zsh rather than drive zsh from bash.

Trade-off: smaller ecosystem than Bats, needs [Revolver](https://github.com/molovo/revolver) as a dependency. Not installed by this repo.

### ShellSpec — full-featured, cross-shell

[ShellSpec](https://github.com/shellspec/shellspec) is a BDD framework that runs on dash, bash, ksh, zsh, and POSIX shells. Supports mocking, parameterised tests, parallel execution, coverage.

Pick ShellSpec when:

- You're shipping a shell library that must work across multiple shells.
- You want RSpec-style `Describe` / `It` / `When` / `The output should …` syntax.
- You need mocking or coverage reports.

Trade-off: heavier to learn than Bats; overkill for simple CLI behaviour checks.

### How to decide

| Situation | Pick |
|-----------|------|
| Bash CLI script, short & simple tests | **Bats** |
| zsh plugin / autoload-heavy code you want tested at the function level | ZUnit |
| Cross-shell library, or need mocking / coverage / BDD | ShellSpec |
| zsh CLI script tested via its external behaviour | **Bats** (drive zsh from bash, assert on output) |

This repo falls in the last row — most "zsh" code here is really "zsh script invoked as a CLI," so Bats is the simplest fit even though the code under test is zsh.

---

## How this repo structures tests

\```
tests/
├── test_helper.bash          # shared helpers, sourced by every .bats file
├── unit/
│   └── zsh_proxy.bats        # fast, no Docker, no network
└── smoke/
    └── docker_install.bats   # runs inside Docker after full install
\```

### `tests/test_helper.bash`

Small helper library (<40 lines). Provides:

- `$REPO_ROOT` — absolute path to the chezmoi source.
- `setup_path_stub` — creates a temp dir and prepends it to `PATH`. Exposes the path via `$BATS_STUB_DIR` (not stdout), so the export survives — **do not wrap it in `$(...)`**. Command substitution runs the helper in a subshell and the `export PATH` is lost.
- `cleanup_path_stubs` — removes any stub dirs registered during the test.
- Default `teardown()` that calls `cleanup_path_stubs`. If a test file defines its own `teardown()`, call `cleanup_path_stubs` at the end to preserve cleanup.

### `tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`

Exercises the proxy helpers in `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh`:

- `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` takes precedence over probing.
- Port probe order: `7890 → 7891 → 1087 → 8118 → 8080`.
- `_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE=none` when nothing responds.
- `__zsh_net_all_proxy_url` returns `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` when set; falls back to the HTTP cache otherwise.
- `proxy-on` exports all six env vars (`http_proxy`, `https_proxy`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`).
- Split HTTP / SOCKS wiring regression guard (commit `fa4c063`).
- `proxy-off` clears all six plus `NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`.
- `proxy-status` exit codes: `1` when unavailable, `0` when available.

Key technique: each test runs `zsh -f -c '...'` (no startup files) so the in-file cache (`$_ZSH_NET_PROXY_CACHE`) can't leak between tests, and `nc` is stubbed via a temp dir on `PATH` — no real network traffic.

### `tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`

Runs inside the Dockerfile-built test image after `chezmoi apply` + ansible have completed. Asserts post-install state:

- `chezmoi apply` is idempotent (re-apply produces empty `chezmoi diff`).
- `zsh -n` passes on `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zshenv`, and every `~/.config/zsh/**/*.zsh`.
- `nvim --headless "+lua print('ok')" +qa` exits 0.
- Core CLI tools on `PATH`: `nvim rg fd fzf zsh just bats`.
- oh-my-zsh plugins present (`zsh-autosuggestions`, `zsh-syntax-highlighting`, `zsh-completions`).
- Unit tests pass under the container's zsh (catches "works on my Mac" regressions).

Invoked by `just docker-test` → `docker compose run --build --rm test` → `bats /tmp/dotfiles-source/tests/smoke`.

---

## Running tests

\```bash
# Fast feedback loop (no Docker, no network, sub-second)
just bats

# Smoke tests inside a clean Ubuntu container (slow — builds image)
just docker-test

# Everything: ansible syntax + pre-commit + bats + docker-test
just check-all
\```

---

## Patterns worth reusing

### Testing zsh code from bats

Bats is bash-based, so drive zsh as a subprocess. Use `zsh -f -c 'source FILE; <call>'` to skip startup files (isolates the code under test) and capture output via `run` or `$(...)`:

\```bash
@test "my zsh function does X" {
  result="$(zsh -f -c "
    source '$REPO_ROOT/dot_config/zsh/tools/my_file.zsh'
    my_function arg1 arg2
  ")"
  [ "$result" = "expected" ]
}
\```

### Stubbing external commands

Prepend a temp dir to `PATH` containing a fake binary:

\```bash
@test "probe order regression" {
  setup_path_stub   # populates $BATS_STUB_DIR, updates $PATH

  cat > "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
port=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do port="$1"; shift; done
[ "$port" = "$EXPECT_PORT" ] && exit 0 || exit 1
EOF
  chmod +x "$BATS_STUB_DIR/nc"

  EXPECT_PORT=1087 zsh -f -c "source '$REPO_ROOT/.../file.zsh'; my_probe"
}
\```

Bats runs every `@test` block in its own subshell, so `PATH` modifications don't leak across tests. `cleanup_path_stubs` (default `teardown`) removes the temp dirs.

### Asserting zsh variables from bash

Inside `zsh -f -c '...'`, use zsh indirect expansion (`${(P)v}`) to print a variable named in another variable:

\```bash
for v in http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy; do
  printf '%s=%s\n' "$v" "${(P)v}"
done
\```

Then bats asserts on the `$output`:

\```bash
[[ "$output" == *"http_proxy=http://test:1234"* ]]
\```

---

## shellcheck + shfmt

[shellcheck](https://www.shellcheck.net/) is a static analyser for shell scripts. [shfmt](https://github.com/mvdan/sh) is a formatter / format-check. Both run via pre-commit in this repo.

Hook scope (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`): **`^scripts/[^/]+\.sh$` only**. This excludes:

- `dot_config/zsh/**/*.zsh` — zsh-specific syntax (`(( ... ))` math, `${(P)v}` expansion flags, `print -u2`, `emulate -L zsh`, `zmodload`) trips shellcheck's bash parser and produces too many false positives.
- `*.sh.tmpl` — chezmoi go-template tokens (`{{ if eq .profile "macos" }}`) look like unbalanced braces to shellcheck.
- `scripts/adhoc/*.sh` — experimental / throwaway scripts by convention.

If a zsh file needs static analysis later, the best options are:

- Run shellcheck with `# shellcheck shell=bash` and manually silence known-false positives — tedious.
- Switch to a zsh-aware linter (there isn't a widely adopted one).
- Or just write a Bats test that covers the behaviour you care about.

Quick commands:

\```bash
# Run only shellcheck on all files
pre-commit run shellcheck --all-files

# Run only shfmt
pre-commit run shfmt --all-files

# shfmt is in diff mode (-d) — to actually rewrite files, install shfmt
# locally and run:
shfmt -i 2 -ci -bn -w scripts/*.sh
\```

---

## Adding a new test

1. Decide unit vs smoke:
   - Pure logic with stub-able inputs → `tests/unit/`.
   - Assertions about post-install system state → `tests/smoke/`.
2. Create `tests/unit/<thing>.bats` (or smoke/). Start with:
   \```bash
   #!/usr/bin/env bats
   load "../test_helper.bash"

   @test "brief description" {
     run some-command
     [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
   }
   \```
3. Run `just bats` (or `just docker-test`) to verify.
4. If the test needs a stub, use `setup_path_stub` + `$BATS_STUB_DIR`.

Rule of thumb for deciding whether a test is worth adding: **would a silent regression here cost me more than ten minutes to diagnose?** If no, skip the test. Personal dotfiles don't need 80% coverage.

## Scan Complete: Shell Functions Worth Testing

Based on my scan of `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/`, here are the functions with meaningful test potential:

### HIGH-VALUE CANDIDATES (pain-if-broken: HIGH)

1. **`ghget`** (41_github.zsh, lines 6–92)
   - Downloads a subdirectory from GitHub tree URL with complex URL parsing
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Parse-heavy (URL splitting, validation) + destructive (downloads, moves files)
   - **What test:** verify URL parsing catches malformed inputs, validates branch/owner/repo extraction, safely extracts subdirs
   - **Regression caught:** silent truncation of branch names, incorrect path splitting, missing validation

2. **`glcreate`** (42_gitlab.zsh, lines 19–40)
   - Creates GitLab repos, sets git remote, and pushes
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - State-changing (git push, remote add), orchestration of multiple commands
   - **What test:** verify remote add/set-url fallback works, branch detection defaults to "main"
   - **Regression caught:** stale origin remotes not updated, wrong branch pushed, git commands fail silently

3. **`pqsum`** (36_pueue.zsh, lines 33–303)
   - Complex jq pipeline processing pueue task status JSON with ETA calculation
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Pure-ish jq logic (high risk of silent bad output), used for monitoring queue health
   - **What test:** verify progress percentage calcs, ETA doesn't go negative, timestamp parsing handles timezones
   - **Regression caught:** negative ETA, incorrect progress %, silent jq parse failure swallowed

4. **`ghostty-ssh-terminfo`** (10_aliases.zsh, lines 61–97)
   - Installs terminfo on remote via SSH with fallback error handling
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Network-facing, checks for missing binaries, piped across SSH
   - **What test:** verify error paths for missing infocmp/tic on remote, local terminfo validation
   - **Regression caught:** remote shell silently swallows tic error, missing binary detection broken

### MEDIUM-VALUE CANDIDATES

5. **`sesh-here` / `sesh-root`** (22_sesh.zsh, lines 48–90)
   - Smart flag parsing (--command, --path) with fallback positional args
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify flag parsing doesn't leak into command, git-root fallback to PWD
   - **Regression caught:** `-c` consumed as command instead of flag, git rev-parse failure crashes instead of fallback

6. **`_tv_history` / tools-picker ZLE widgets** (12_television.zsh, 11_tools_picker.zsh)
   - Interactive ZLE widgets (harder to test, but state-dependent)
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify `_tools_list` awk regex correctly parses markdown pipes, trailing space preservation
   - **Regression caught:** backtick stripping broken, tab delimiter mangled

7. **`readurl` / `readlocal` / `readraw`** (55_web_reader.zsh, lines 32–81)
   - URL normalization + binary dependency checks + proxy fallback
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify _norm_url prepends https:// only when needed, binary check doesn't shadow failures
   - **Regression caught:** invalid URLs not normalized, missing binary error silently suppressed

### LOW-VALUE / OUT OF SCOPE

- `_ssh_add_probe`, `_try_bitwarden_agent`, `_existing_agent_works` (94_ssh_agent.zsh) — already tested via implicit startup logic, timeout handling complex but tested on real sockets
- `try-sesh`, `sesh-sessions` — mostly orchestration of existing tools

- `_conda_init` — lazy-loading wrapper, pure init code
- All aliases and PATH setup (02_legacy_tools.zsh, 06_cargo.zsh, etc.) — out of scope
- Simple config sourcing (30_direnv.zsh, 25_bat.zsh, etc.) — "NONE" category

---

## TOP 3 RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **`ghget`** — Most painful regression risk. Parse-heavy URL logic, destructive (downloads/moves files), silent failure on malformed URLs. Start here.

2. **`pqsum`** — High logic density (60+ lines of jq), used for daily queue monitoring, silent bad output (wrong ETA) undermines workflow.

3. **`glcreate`** — Git state changes, branch detection critical, remote fallback logic (add vs set-url) is brittle.

All three protect against high-impact silent failures. Skip the rest unless you add more orchestration complexity.

1	# 42_gitlab.zsh - GitLab helpers using glab CLI
2	
3	# ==============================================================================
4	# Method 1: Direct shell function (no AI agent needed)
5	# ==============================================================================
6	
7	# Create a GitLab repo under a group from the current git repo, set origin, and push.
8	# Detects current folder name as repo name and current branch automatically.
9	#
10	# Usage:
11	#   glcreate <group> [description]
12	#
13	# Examples:
14	#   glcreate david_quick_tries
15	#   glcreate david_quick_tries "My awesome project"
16	#
17	# If no description is given, the repo is created without one.
18	# The repo is created as private by default.
19	glcreate() {
20	  emulate -L zsh
21	
22	  local group="${1:?Usage: glcreate <group> [description]}"
23	  local desc="${2:-}"
24	  local name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
25	  local branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
26	
27	  echo "Creating: ${group}/${name} (branch: ${branch})"
28	
29	  glab repo create "${group}/${name}" \
30	    --private \
31	    --defaultBranch "$branch" \
32	    --skipGitInit \
33	    ${desc:+--description "$desc"} \
34	  && {
35	    # Add or update origin remote
36	    git remote add origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git" 2>/dev/null \
37	      || git remote set-url origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git"
38	  } \
39	  && git push -u origin "$branch"
40	}
41	
42	# ==============================================================================
43	# Method 2: AI agent assisted (summarizes description from project content)
44	# ==============================================================================
45	
46	# Create a GitLab repo using an AI coding agent to inspect the project,
47	# auto-generate a description, create the repo, set origin, and push.
48	#
49	# Supported agents: opencode (default), claude, codex, cursor-agent
50	# Set GLCREATE_AGENT to change the default agent.
51	# Set GLCREATE_LANG to change the default prompt language (zh or en, default: zh).
52	#
53	# Usage:
54	#   glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent <name>] [--lang zh|en]
55	#
56	# Examples:
57	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries
58	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries "Override description"
59	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --agent claude
60	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --lang en
61	#
62	# If no description is given, the agent will summarize one from the project content.
63	glcreate-ai() {
64	  emulate -L zsh
65	
66	  local group="" desc="" agent="${GLCREATE_AGENT:-opencode}" lang="${GLCREATE_LANG:-zh}"
67	
68	  # Parse arguments
69	  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
70	    case "$1" in
71	      --agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
72	      --lang)  lang="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	      *) [[ -z "$group" ]] && group="$1" || desc="$1"; shift ;;
74	    esac
75	  done
76	
77	  if [[ -z "$group" ]]; then
78	    echo "Usage: glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent opencode|claude|codex|cursor-agent] [--lang zh|en]"
79	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_AGENT env var to change default agent (default: opencode)"
80	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_LANG  env var to change default language (default: zh)"
81	    return 1
82	  fi
83	
84	  local name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
85	  local branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
86	  local prompt
87	
88	  case "$lang" in
89	    en)
90	      prompt="Use glab to create a private repo under gitlab.com/${group}, repo name: ${name}, default branch: ${branch}. Set the origin remote and push.${desc:+ Description: ${desc}.} If no description is provided, summarize one sentence from the project content."
91	      ;;
92	    zh|*)
93	      prompt="用 glab 把這個 repo 建到 gitlab.com/${group} 底下，repo name: ${name}，private，default branch: ${branch}，設定 origin remote 並 push。${desc:+Description: ${desc}。}如果沒給 description 就根據項目內容總結一句。"
94	      ;;
95	  esac
96	
97	  echo "Agent: ${agent} | Lang: ${lang} | Repo: ${group}/${name} | Branch: ${branch}"
98	
99	  case "$agent" in
100	    opencode)       opencode run "$prompt" ;;
101	    claude)         claude -p "$prompt" ;;
102	    codex)          codex exec "$prompt" ;;
103	    cursor-agent)   cursor-agent -p "$prompt" ;;
104	    *)              echo "Unknown agent: ${agent}"; return 1 ;;
105	  esac
106	}

19	# Parse the markdown tables into "INVOCATION<TAB>DESCRIPTION" lines.

24	      desc=$4; sub(/^[[:space:]]*/,"",desc); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/,"",desc)

260	    printf '  Total tasks: %s\n' "$overall_total"
261	    printf '  Done progress: %s/%s  %s  %s\n' "$overall_done" "$overall_total" "$overall_bar" "$overall_pct"
262	    printf '  Avg done duration: %s\n' "$overall_avg"
263	    printf '  Est. remaining (ETA): %s\n' "$overall_eta"
264	
265	    printf '\n%sStatus Breakdown%s\n' "$c_title" "$c_reset"
266	    local status_count
267	    status_count="$(jq -r '.status_rows | length' <<< "$stats_json")"
268	    if (( status_count == 0 )); then
269	        printf '  -\n'
270	    else
271	        {
272	            printf 'status\tcount\tprogress\n'
273	            jq -r '.status_rows[] | "\(.status)\t\(.count)\t\(.pct)"' <<< "$stats_json"
274	        } | pqsum_align_table | sed 's/^/  /'
275	    fi
276	
277	    printf '\n%sGroup Summary%s\n' "$c_title" "$c_reset"
278	    local group_count
279	    group_count="$(jq -r '.group_rows | length' <<< "$stats_json")"
280	    if (( group_count == 0 )); then
281	        printf '  -\n'
282	    else
283	        {
284	            printf 'group\tdaemon\tparallel\ttotal\tdone\tprogress\tbar\ttotal_spent\tavg_done\teta\tstatuses\n'
285	            while IFS=$'\t' read -r group daemon parallel total done pct pct_int total_spent avg_done eta statuses; do
286	                printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
287	                    "$group" \
288	                    "$daemon" \
289	                    "$parallel" \
290	                    "$total" \
291	                    "$done" \
292	                    "$pct" \
293	                    "$(pqsum_progress_bar "$pct_int")" \
294	                    "$total_spent" \
295	                    "$avg_done" \
296	                    "$eta" \
297	                    "$statuses"
298	            done < <(
299	                jq -r '.group_rows[] | "\(.group)\t\(.daemon)\t\(.parallel)\t\(.total)\t\(.done)\t\(.pct)\t\(.pct_int)\t\(.total_spent)\t\(.avg_done)\t\(.eta)\t\(.statuses)"' <<< "$stats_json"
300	            )
301	        } | pqsum_align_table | sed 's/^/  /'
302	    fi

1	# 55_web_reader.zsh - Render web pages as markdown in the terminal
2	#
3	# Four extractors, pick by function name:
4	#   readurl   - jina.ai Reader (remote, zero local deps beyond glow)
5	#   readlocal - trafilatura (local, Python; offline article extraction)
6	#   readnode  - readability-cli / `readable` (local, Node; Mozilla Readability)
7	#   readraw   - curl + pandoc (full page -> GFM; no article extraction)
8	#
9	# All wrap the underlying fetch in `try_direct_then_proxy` from 50_networking.zsh,
10	# so non-GFW'd URLs pay zero proxy overhead and only fall back if direct fetch fails.
11	
12	# Normalize URL: prepend https:// if scheme missing.
13	_norm_url() {
14	  local url="$1"
15	  if [[ "$url" != http://* && "$url" != https://* ]]; then
16	    url="https://$url"
17	  fi
18	  printf '%s\n' "$url"
19	}
20	
21	# Missing-binary guard: print a one-line install hint and return 127.
22	__zsh_reader_require() {
23	  local bin="$1" hint="$2"
24	  if ! command -v "$bin" &>/dev/null; then
25	    print -u2 "$bin not found -- install: $hint"
26	    return 127
27	  fi
28	  return 0
29	}
30	
31	# readurl <url> - jina.ai Reader + glow. The default convenience.
32	readurl() {
33	  local raw="$1"
34	  if [[ -z "$raw" ]]; then
35	    print -u2 "usage: readurl <url>"
36	    return 2
37	  fi
38	  __zsh_reader_require glow "brew install glow  (or the devtools ansible role)" || return
39	  local url; url="$(_norm_url "$raw")"
40	  try_direct_then_proxy glow -p "https://r.jina.ai/$url"
41	}
42	
43	# readlocal <url> - trafilatura (offline article extraction) + glow.
44	readlocal() {
45	  local raw="$1"
46	  if [[ -z "$raw" ]]; then
47	    print -u2 "usage: readlocal <url>"
48	    return 2
49	  fi
50	  __zsh_reader_require trafilatura "uv tool install trafilatura  (or enable the python_uv_tools ansible role)" || return
51	  __zsh_reader_require glow "brew install glow  (or the devtools ansible role)" || return
52	  local url; url="$(_norm_url "$raw")"
53	  try_direct_then_proxy trafilatura -u "$url" --markdown | glow -
54	}
55

57	readnode() {

64	  __zsh_reader_require glow "brew install glow  (or the devtools ansible role)" || return
65	  local url; url="$(_norm_url "$raw")"

1	# 94_ssh_agent.zsh - SSH agent with Bitwarden-first fallback to ssh-agent
2	#
3	# Priority order:
4	#   1. Bitwarden SSH agent (desktop app socket)
5	#   2. Existing SSH_AUTH_SOCK (e.g. forwarded agent, systemd, gnome-keyring)
6	#   3. Persistent ssh-agent (spawned once per user, reused across shells)
7	#
8	# The fallback ssh-agent uses a fixed socket path so multiple shells share
9	# one agent instead of spawning a new one each time.
10	
11	# Probe timeout (seconds) — keeps shell startup fast even when an agent
12	# socket exists but the daemon behind it is hung or locked.
13	_SSH_AGENT_PROBE_TIMEOUT=2
14	
15	# Wrapper: ssh-add -l with a timeout to avoid hanging on unresponsive sockets.
16	# Returns the same exit codes as ssh-add -l (0, 1, 2) plus 124 for timeout.
17	_ssh_add_probe() {
18	    if command -v timeout &>/dev/null; then
19	        timeout "$_SSH_AGENT_PROBE_TIMEOUT" ssh-add -l "$@" 2>&1
20	    else
21	        # No timeout command (rare) — run directly and hope for the best
22	        ssh-add -l "$@" 2>&1
23	    fi
24	}
25	
26	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
27	# 1. Try Bitwarden SSH agent
28	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
29	_try_bitwarden_agent() {
30	    typeset -a _bw_candidates
31	
32	    if [[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]]; then
33	        _bw_candidates=(
34	            "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Bitwarden/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
35	            "$HOME/Library/Containers/com.bitwarden.desktop/Data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
36	            "$HOME/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
37	        )
38	    else
39	        _bw_candidates=(
40	            "$HOME/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
41	            "$HOME/snap/bitwarden/current/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
42	            "$HOME/.var/app/com.bitwarden.desktop/data/.bitwarden-ssh-agent.sock"
43	        )
44	    fi
45	
46	    for _sock in "${_bw_candidates[@]}"; do
47	        if [[ -S "$_sock" ]]; then
48	            # Socket file exists — verify the agent actually responds
49	            local _out
50	            _out="$(SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock" _ssh_add_probe)"
51	            local rc=$?
52	            # rc=0: keys listed  → usable
53	            # rc=1 + "no identities": agent ok, no keys loaded → usable
54	            # rc=1 + "refused": Bitwarden locked/agent disabled → skip
55	            # rc=2: agent unreachable → skip
56	            # rc=124: timed out → skip
57	            if (( rc == 0 )); then
58	                export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock"
59	                return 0
60	            elif (( rc == 1 )) && [[ "$_out" != *"refused"* ]]; then
61	                export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$_sock"
62	                return 0
63	            fi
64	        fi
65	    done
66	    return 1
67	}
68	
69	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
70	# 2. Check if the current SSH_AUTH_SOCK is already usable
71	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
72	_existing_agent_works() {
73	    [[ -n "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" && -S "$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" ]] || return 1
74	    local _out
75	    _out="$(_ssh_add_probe)"
76	    local rc=$?
77	    # Accept rc=0 (keys) or rc=1 without "refused" (empty but alive)
78	    if (( rc == 0 )); then
79	        return 0
80	    elif (( rc == 1 )) && [[ "$_out" != *"refused"* ]]; then
81	        return 0
82	    fi
83	    return 1
84	}
85	
86	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
87	# 3. Fallback: persistent ssh-agent with a well-known socket
88	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	_fallback_ssh_agent() {
90	    local agent_dir="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-$HOME/.cache}/ssh-agent"
91	    local agent_sock="$agent_dir/agent.sock"
92	    local agent_pid_file="$agent_dir/agent.pid"
93	
94	    # Reuse existing persistent agent if it's alive
95	    if [[ -S "$agent_sock" ]]; then
96	        export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$agent_sock"
97	        if [[ -f "$agent_pid_file" ]]; then
98	            export SSH_AGENT_PID="$(< "$agent_pid_file")"
99	        fi
100	        # Verify it actually works
101	        _ssh_add_probe &>/dev/null
102	        local rc=$?
103	        if (( rc == 0 || rc == 1 )); then
104	            _maybe_add_keys
105	            return 0
106	        fi
107	        # Stale socket — clean up and respawn below
108	        rm -f "$agent_sock" "$agent_pid_file"
109	    fi
110	
111	    # Spawn a new agent with a fixed socket path
112	    mkdir -p "$agent_dir"
113	    chmod 700 "$agent_dir"
114	    eval "$(ssh-agent -a "$agent_sock" 2>/dev/null)" &>/dev/null
115	    if [[ -n "$SSH_AGENT_PID" ]]; then
116	        echo "$SSH_AGENT_PID" > "$agent_pid_file"
117	        export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$agent_sock"
118	        _maybe_add_keys
119	        return 0
120	    fi
121	    return 1
122	}
123	
124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
125	# Auto-add keys that exist on disk (only when agent has no identities)
126	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
127	_maybe_add_keys() {
128	    # Only add if agent is empty
129	    ssh-add -l &>/dev/null
130	    (( $? == 1 )) || return 0  # rc=1 means "agent ok, no identities"
131	
132	    # Common private key names (add more as needed)
133	    local -a key_names=(id_ed25519 id_rsa id_ecdsa jingle)
134	    for k in "${key_names[@]}"; do
135	        local kf="$HOME/.ssh/$k"
136	        [[ -f "$kf" ]] && SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=never ssh-add -q "$kf" 2>/dev/null
137	    done
138	}
139	
140	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	# Main: try each strategy in order
142	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143	_try_bitwarden_agent || _existing_agent_works || _fallback_ssh_agent
144	
145	# Clean up helper functions (they pollute the namespace)
146	unfunction _try_bitwarden_agent _existing_agent_works _fallback_ssh_agent _maybe_add_keys _ssh_add_probe 2>/dev/null
147	unset _SSH_AGENT_PROBE_TIMEOUT
148

1	# 12_television.zsh - Television (tv) shell integration
2	#
3	# Tab completion via ~/.zfunc/_tv (regenerated on version change).
4	# We do NOT use `tv init zsh` because it binds Ctrl+T and Ctrl+R,
5	# which conflict with fzf's shell integration.
6	#
7	# Instead, tv channels are bound to Alt keys:
8	#   Alt+R  tv shell history     (tv-style history search)
9	#   Alt+P  tv files             (tv-style file/path picker)
10	#   Alt+G  tv git-log           (git log browser)
11	#   Alt+E  tv env               (environment variables)
12	#   Alt+A  tv aliases           (all aliases & functions)
13	#
14	# fzf keeps Ctrl+T / Ctrl+R / Alt+C (muscle memory).
15	# tv gets Alt namespace for advanced pickers.
16	#
17	# Aliases cache: ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt is generated on shell startup
18	# so that `tv aliases` channel can read it without spawning `zsh -ic`
19	# (which causes tty suspend issues).
20	#
21	# See: https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television
22	
23	command -v tv &>/dev/null || return 0
24	
25	# --- Tab completion (written to ~/.zfunc/, picked up by compinit) ---
26	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
27	  local _tv_ver="$(tv --version 2>/dev/null)"
28	  if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_tv ]] || ! grep -q "${_tv_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null; then
29	    tv completions zsh > ~/.zfunc/_tv 2>/dev/null
30	  fi
31	fi
32	
33	# --- Generate aliases cache for tv aliases channel ---
34	{
35	  mkdir -p ~/.cache/tv
36	  {
37	    alias | while IFS="=" read -r name rest; do
38	      printf "%-22s  alias   %s\n" "$name" "$rest"
39	    done
40	    typeset -f + | while read -r name; do
41	      printf "%-22s  func\n" "$name"
42	    done
43	  } | sort > ~/.cache/tv/aliases.txt
44	} &>/dev/null &!
45	
46	# --- Custom ZLE widgets for tv channels ---
47	
48	_tv_channel_widget() {
49	  emulate -L zsh
50	  zle -I
51	  local output
52	  output=$(tv "$1" --no-status-bar --inline < /dev/tty)
53	  zle reset-prompt
54	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
55	    LBUFFER+="$output"
56	  fi
57	}
58	
59	_tv_history() {
60	  emulate -L zsh
61	  zle -I
62	  local output current_prompt
63	  current_prompt=$LBUFFER
64	  output=$(history -n -1 0 | tv --no-status-bar --input "$current_prompt" --inline < /dev/tty)
65	  zle reset-prompt
66	  if [[ -n $output ]]; then
67	    RBUFFER=""
68	    LBUFFER="$output"
69	  fi
70	}
71	
72	_tv_files()   { _tv_channel_widget "files"; }
73	_tv_gitlog()  { _tv_channel_widget "git-log"; }
74	_tv_env()     { _tv_channel_widget "env"; }
75	_tv_aliases() { _tv_channel_widget "aliases"; }
76	
77	zle -N tv-history  _tv_history
78	zle -N tv-files    _tv_files
79	zle -N tv-gitlog   _tv_gitlog
80	zle -N tv-env      _tv_env
81	zle -N tv-aliases  _tv_aliases
82	
83	# --- Keybindings (Alt namespace) ---
84	# Note: Alt+F is reserved for forward-word (emacs mode default).
85	bindkey '\er' tv-history   # Alt+R
86	bindkey '\ep' tv-files     # Alt+P (path/pick)
87	bindkey '\eg' tv-gitlog    # Alt+G
88	bindkey '\ee' tv-env       # Alt+E
89	bindkey '\ea' tv-aliases   # Alt+A

4	# Check if sesh is installed
5	command -v sesh &>/dev/null || return 0

7	# Auto-generate shell completion into ~/.zfunc/ (regenerates on version change)
8	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]]; then
9	    local _sesh_ver="$(sesh --version 2>/dev/null)"
10	    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_sesh ]] || ! grep -q "${_sesh_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null; then
11	        sesh completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_sesh 2>/dev/null
12	    fi
13	fi
14	
15	# Sesh session switcher with fzf (full-featured picker)
16	# Supports icons, preview, filtering by source, and session killing
17	function sesh-sessions() {
18	    {
19	        exec </dev/tty
20	        exec <&1
21	        local session
22	        session=$(sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
23	            --no-sort --ansi --border-label ' sesh ' --prompt '⚡  ' \
24	            --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^d tmux kill ^f find' \
25	            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
26	            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
27	            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
28	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
29	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
30	            --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
31	            --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
32	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
33	            --preview 'sesh preview {}' \
34	        )
35	        zle reset-prompt > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
36	        [[ -z "$session" ]] && return
37	        sesh connect "$session"
38	    }
39	}
40	
41	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
42	# Smart argument handling:
43	#   shere                              # default startup_command (nvim)
44	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
45	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
46	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path
47	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
48	function sesh-here() {
49	    local cmd="" path=""
50	    # Parse flags first
51	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
52	        case "$1" in
53	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
54	            -p|--path)    path="$2"; shift 2 ;;
55	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
56	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
57	        esac
58	    done
59	    # Remaining positional args become the command
60	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
61	    path="${path:-$PWD}"
62	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
63	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$path"
64	    else
65	        sesh connect "$path"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
70	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
71	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
72	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
73	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
74	function sesh-root() {
75	    local cmd="" root
76	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
77	        case "$1" in
78	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	            -*)           shift ;;
80	            *)            break ;;
81	        esac
82	    done
83	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
84	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
85	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
86	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
87	    else
88	        sesh connect "$root"
89	    fi
90	}
91	
92	alias shere='sesh-here'
93	alias sroot='sesh-root'

99	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
100	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
101	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions

18	# ── try + sesh integration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
19	# Open a try project and immediately start a sesh coding session.

22	#   try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo  # clone, then sesh connect
23	#
24	# The session name follows sesh's dir_length=2 convention:
25	#   e.g. "tries/2026-04-14-some-project"
26	function try-sesh() {

29	        return 1
30	    fi
31	    # Run try, which cd's into the project directory
32	    try "$@" || return $?
33	    # Now connect sesh to the directory try landed in
34	    sesh connect "$PWD"
35	}

37	alias tsesh='try-sesh'

1	# 41_github.zsh - GitHub URL helpers
2	
3	# Download a subdirectory from a GitHub repository tree URL.
4	# Example:
5	#   ghget https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/tree/high-freq-execution/examples/trade/
6	ghget() {
7	  emulate -L zsh
8	  setopt localoptions pipefail
9	
10	  local usage="Usage: ghget https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<branch>/<path>"
11	  local branch_note="ghget currently supports only GitHub tree URLs with a single-segment branch name (no '/' in branch)."
12	
13	  if (( $# != 1 )); then
14	    print -u2 -- "$usage"
15	    print -u2 -- "$branch_note"
16	    return 1
17	  fi
18	
19	  local url="$1"
20	  local prefix="https://github.com/"
21	  if [[ "$url" != ${prefix}* ]]; then
22	    print -u2 -- "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $url"
23	    print -u2 -- "$usage"
24	    print -u2 -- "$branch_note"
25	    return 1
26	  fi
27	
28	  url="${url#$prefix}"
29	  url="${url%%\?*}"
30	  url="${url%%\#*}"
31	  url="${url%/}"
32	
33	  local -a parts
34	  parts=(${(s:/:)url})
35	  if (( ${#parts} < 5 )) || [[ "${parts[3]}" != "tree" ]]; then
36	    print -u2 -- "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $1"
37	    print -u2 -- "$usage"
38	    print -u2 -- "$branch_note"
39	    return 1
40	  fi
41	
42	  local owner="${parts[1]}"
43	  local repo="${parts[2]}"
44	  local branch="${parts[4]}"
45	  local subdir_path="${(j:/:)parts[5,-1]}"
46	  local leaf="${subdir_path:t}"
47	
48	  if [[ -z "$owner" || -z "$repo" || -z "$branch" || -z "$subdir_path" || -z "$leaf" ]]; then
49	    print -u2 -- "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $1"
50	    print -u2 -- "$usage"
51	    print -u2 -- "$branch_note"
52	    return 1
53	  fi
54	
55	  if [[ -e "$leaf" ]]; then
56	    print -u2 -- "Destination already exists: $PWD/$leaf"
57	    return 1
58	  fi
59	
60	  local -a path_parts
61	  path_parts=(${(s:/:)subdir_path})
62	  local strip="${#path_parts}"
63	  local archive_root="${repo}-${branch}"
64	  local tmpdir
65	  tmpdir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ghget.XXXXXX")" || {
66	    print -u2 -- "Failed to create temporary directory"
67	    return 1
68	  }
69	
70	  print -- "Downloading $owner/$repo/$subdir_path (branch: $branch) ..."
71	  if ! command curl -fsSL "https://github.com/$owner/$repo/archive/refs/heads/$branch.tar.gz" \
72	    | command tar -xz -C "$tmpdir" --strip-components="$strip" -f - "$archive_root/$subdir_path"; then
73	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
74	    print -u2 -- "Failed to download or extract '$subdir_path' from '$owner/$repo' on branch '$branch'"
75	    print -u2 -- "$branch_note"
76	    return 1
77	  fi
78	
79	  if [[ ! -d "$tmpdir/$leaf" ]]; then
80	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
81	    print -u2 -- "Expected extracted directory was not found: $leaf"
82	    return 1
83	  fi
84	
85	  if ! command mv -- "$tmpdir/$leaf" .; then
86	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
87	    print -u2 -- "Failed to move extracted directory into: $PWD"
88	    return 1
89	  fi
90	
91	  command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
92	}
93

Based on my scan of `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/zsh/`, here are the functions with meaningful test potential:

### HIGH-VALUE CANDIDATES (pain-if-broken: HIGH)

1. **`ghget`** (41_github.zsh, lines 6–92)
   - Downloads a subdirectory from GitHub tree URL with complex URL parsing
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Parse-heavy (URL splitting, validation) + destructive (downloads, moves files)
   - **What test:** verify URL parsing catches malformed inputs, validates branch/owner/repo extraction, safely extracts subdirs
   - **Regression caught:** silent truncation of branch names, incorrect path splitting, missing validation

2. **`glcreate`** (42_gitlab.zsh, lines 19–40)
   - Creates GitLab repos, sets git remote, and pushes
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - State-changing (git push, remote add), orchestration of multiple commands
   - **What test:** verify remote add/set-url fallback works, branch detection defaults to "main"
   - **Regression caught:** stale origin remotes not updated, wrong branch pushed, git commands fail silently

3. **`pqsum`** (36_pueue.zsh, lines 33–303)
   - Complex jq pipeline processing pueue task status JSON with ETA calculation
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Pure-ish jq logic (high risk of silent bad output), used for monitoring queue health
   - **What test:** verify progress percentage calcs, ETA doesn't go negative, timestamp parsing handles timezones
   - **Regression caught:** negative ETA, incorrect progress %, silent jq parse failure swallowed

4. **`ghostty-ssh-terminfo`** (10_aliases.zsh, lines 61–97)
   - Installs terminfo on remote via SSH with fallback error handling
   - Testability: **HIGH** | Pain-if-broken: **high**
   - Network-facing, checks for missing binaries, piped across SSH
   - **What test:** verify error paths for missing infocmp/tic on remote, local terminfo validation
   - **Regression caught:** remote shell silently swallows tic error, missing binary detection broken

### MEDIUM-VALUE CANDIDATES

5. **`sesh-here` / `sesh-root`** (22_sesh.zsh, lines 48–90)
   - Smart flag parsing (--command, --path) with fallback positional args
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify flag parsing doesn't leak into command, git-root fallback to PWD
   - **Regression caught:** `-c` consumed as command instead of flag, git rev-parse failure crashes instead of fallback

6. **`_tv_history` / tools-picker ZLE widgets** (12_television.zsh, 11_tools_picker.zsh)
   - Interactive ZLE widgets (harder to test, but state-dependent)
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify `_tools_list` awk regex correctly parses markdown pipes, trailing space preservation
   - **Regression caught:** backtick stripping broken, tab delimiter mangled

7. **`readurl` / `readlocal` / `readraw`** (55_web_reader.zsh, lines 32–81)
   - URL normalization + binary dependency checks + proxy fallback
   - Testability: **MEDIUM** | Pain-if-broken: **medium**
   - **What test:** verify _norm_url prepends https:// only when needed, binary check doesn't shadow failures
   - **Regression caught:** invalid URLs not normalized, missing binary error silently suppressed

### LOW-VALUE / OUT OF SCOPE

- `_ssh_add_probe`, `_try_bitwarden_agent`, `_existing_agent_works` (94_ssh_agent.zsh) — already tested via implicit startup logic, timeout handling complex but tested on real sockets
- `try-sesh`, `sesh-sessions` — mostly orchestration of existing tools
- `glcreate-ai` — delegates to external AI agents, not pure logic
- `_conda_init` — lazy-loading wrapper, pure init code
- All aliases and PATH setup (02_legacy_tools.zsh, 06_cargo.zsh, etc.) — out of scope
- Simple config sourcing (30_direnv.zsh, 25_bat.zsh, etc.) — "NONE" category

---

## TOP 3 RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **`ghget`** — Most painful regression risk. Parse-heavy URL logic, destructive (downloads/moves files), silent failure on malformed URLs. Start here.

2. **`pqsum`** — High logic density (60+ lines of jq), used for daily queue monitoring, silent bad output (wrong ETA) undermines workflow.

3. **`glcreate`** — Git state changes, branch detection critical, remote fallback logic (add vs set-url) is brittle.

All three protect against high-impact silent failures. Skip the rest unless you add more orchestration complexity.
